@activityAnsweredIn.description: The second line of a step where the person allowed or denied what the agent asked: how long they took to answer. duration is as "14 s" or "1 min 02 s".

@activityApprovals.description: Under a task's outcome on its row in Activity: how many times the task asked the person to allow something.

activityChooseTask: Choose a task to see its steps.

@activityChooseTask.description: Activity's right column when no task is selected.

@activityDelete.description: An item of the ⋯ menu in a task's detail, which deletes the task. It shows disabled: the gateway cannot delete one task yet.

@activityDetailLabel.description: The accessibility label of Activity's right column: the selected task's detail.

@activityEmpty.description: Activity's list when no task has finished yet.

@activityMoreActions.description: The accessibility label of the ⋯ button in a task's detail, whose menu has Export…, Step-by-step replay and Delete.

@activityNoMatch.description: Activity's list when the search finds nothing. query is what the person typed.

@activityOutcomeDenied.description: A task's outcome on its row in Activity, a state: the task ended after the person denied what it asked.

@activityOutcomeDone.description: A task's outcome on its row in Activity, a state: the task finished.

@activityOutcomeFailed.description: A task's outcome on its row in Activity, a state: the task failed.

@activityOutcomeStopped.description: A task's outcome on its row in Activity, a state: the person or the agent stopped it.

@activityPanelClose.description: The button in the header of Watch replay and of Watch recording that closes them, back to the task's steps.

@activityReadFailed.description: A toast when Activity cannot load the finished tasks from the gateway. detail is the error, in English.

@activitySearchLabel.description: The accessibility label of Activity's search field.

@activitySearchPlaceholder.description: The placeholder of Activity's search field, which finds tasks by their titles and apps as the person types.

@activityShowShot.description: The tooltip of a step's screenshot thumbnail: a click shows it larger, below the step.

@activityStepShotLabel.description: The accessibility label of a step's screenshot thumbnail, a button that shows the screenshot larger. step is the step's text.

@activitySteps.description: The heading above the list of a task's steps in Activity's detail.

@activityTasksLabel.description: The accessibility label of Activity's left column: the list of finished tasks.

@activityTitle.description: The title in the Activity page's header. Activity lists the finished tasks by day.

@addAndroidBrandQuestion.description: Add phone › Android: the label above the row of phone brands to pick from; the steps below follow the brand picked.

addAndroidDetail: Pinky works with Android 10 and later. Pick your phone's brand and follow its steps: Pinky finds the phone as soon as it's ready.

@addAndroidDetail.description: Add phone › Android: the line under the heading.

addAndroidFoundAllow: Found {name}. Unlock it and tap Allow on the phone.

@addAndroidFoundAllow.description: Add phone › Android, step 3: next to a spinner once the phone shows up but has not allowed this computer yet.

addAndroidNamesDiffer: Menu names change between models and system versions: where yours differ, go by the names on your phone.

@addAndroidNamesDiffer.description: Add phone › Android: a small note under the brands, since the menu names in the steps may differ from the person's phone.

addAndroidNoPrompt: No prompt on the phone? Unplug it and plug it in again; if the phone asks what to use USB for, pick File transfer. Still nothing: in Developer options, tap Revoke USB debugging authorizations (on Android 17: Revoke adb debugging authorizations), then plug it in again.

@addAndroidNoPrompt.description: Add phone › Android, step 3, and the checkup: what to try when the phone shows no prompt to allow this computer. File transfer and Revoke USB debugging authorizations are Android's own names: use those of Android's Simplified Chinese settings.

addAndroidNoWirelessDebugging: This phone has no Wireless debugging. To use it without the cable, keep it on this computer's Wi-Fi:

@addAndroidNoWirelessDebugging.description: Add phone › Android, last step, for a phone without Wireless debugging on a cable: above the button wiFiUse.

addAndroidNotSeen: Nothing yet? Check that USB debugging is on, unlock the phone, and try another cable or port.

@addAndroidNotSeen.description: Add phone › Android, step 3: under the spinner while no phone shows up.

@addAndroidOffline.description: Add phone › Android, step 3: the phone showed up but is offline or in another mode; the system's words follow.

addAndroidRecognized: Pinky recognized {system} on {name}: these are its steps.

@addAndroidRecognized.description: Add phone › Android: shown under the brands once the phone is connected and Pinky switched the steps to its maker.

addAndroidRecognizedPhone: Pinky recognized {name}: these are its steps.

@addAndroidRecognizedPhone.description: Add phone › Android: as addAndroidRecognized, for a phone whose system has no name of its own (a Pixel).

@addAndroidSketchAllow.description: Add phone › Android, step 3: the drawn prompt's button to tap, as Android words it.

@addAndroidSketchAlways.description: Add phone › Android, step 3: the check box of the drawn prompt, as Android words it: use the words of Android's Simplified Chinese prompt.

@addAndroidSketchCancel.description: Add phone › Android, step 3: the drawn prompt's first button, as Android words it.

@addAndroidSketchLabel.description: Add phone › Android, step 3: the accessible name of the drawing of the phone's prompt.

@addAndroidSketchTitle.description: Add phone › Android, step 3: the title of the drawn prompt, as Android words it: use the words of Android's Simplified Chinese prompt.

@addAndroidStepCheck.description: Add phone › Android, step 4's title: the phone's checkup.

addAndroidStepCheckDetail: Pinky checks, item by item, that it can see the screen, tap and type.

@addAndroidStepCheckDetail.description: Add phone › Android, step 4: above the checkup's items.

@addAndroidStepDev.description: Add phone › Android, step 1's title. Developer options is Android's own name: use that of Android's Simplified Chinese settings.

addAndroidStepDevTap: Tap {item} 7 times, until the phone says you're now a developer. If it asks, enter your lock screen password.

@addAndroidStepDevTap.description: Add phone › Android, step 1: under the menu path to the item. item is the name of the item to tap, as the phone's maker calls it.

addAndroidStepPlug: Plug in the phone and allow this computer
addAndroidStepPlugDetail: Plug the phone into this computer with a USB cable that carries data. When the phone asks, tick the box and tap {button}:

@addAndroidStepPlugDetail.description: Add phone › Android, step 3: above a drawing of the phone's "Allow USB debugging?" prompt. button is the prompt's button, as the phone's maker words it (Allow, or OK on HUAWEI and HONOR phones).

@addAndroidStepUSB.description: Add phone › Android, step 2's title. USB debugging is Android's own name: use that of Android's Simplified Chinese settings.

addAndroidStepsLabel: Steps to connect an Android phone

@addAndroidStepsLabel.description: Add phone › Android: the accessible name of the list of steps.

addAndroidTailnet: Phone not on this network? Use Tailscale

@addAndroidTailnet.description: Add phone › Android: the link next to addPhoneOrWiFi that opens the steps to connect a phone through Tailscale, for a phone away from this computer's network. Tailscale and tailnet are product words: keep them.

@addAndroidTitle.description: Add phone › Android: the heading of the steps that prepare and connect an Android phone.

@addAndroidTurnOff.description: Add phone › Android, step 2: one switch to turn off (Samsung's Auto Blocker). name is the switch's name on the phone.

@addAndroidTurnOn.description: Add phone › Android, step 2: one switch to turn on in Developer options. name is the switch's name on the phone.

@addPhoneBack.description: Add phone: the link at the top left of the wizard that goes back a step.

@addPhoneCancel.description: Add phone: the button at the top right of the wizard that leaves it.

@addPhoneChooseAndroid.description: Add phone, first step: under "Android" on its card, examples of Android phones.

addPhoneChooseDetail: Pinky works with Android phones and iPhones.

@addPhoneChooseDetail.description: Add phone, first step: the line under the heading.

addPhoneChooseIPhone: Best on iOS 27; older versions work too

@addPhoneChooseIPhone.description: Add phone, first step: under "iPhone" on its card, which iOS versions work.

@addPhoneChooseTitle.description: Add phone, first step: the heading above two cards to pick from, Android and iPhone.

@addPhoneDone.description: Add phone: the button that ends the wizard once the new phone is ready, and opens its page.

@addPhoneFound.description: Add phone: the status line once Pinky has found the new Android phone and it is ready, next to a green dot. name is the phone's name.

@addPhoneFoundIOS.description: Add phone › iPhone: the status line once Pinky has found the iPhone, before it is ready. name is the iPhone's name; version is its iOS version, or empty (the line then ends with "iOS").

addPhoneIPhoneAnother: To add another iPhone, plug it in.

@addPhoneIPhoneAnother.description: Add phone › iPhone: a note under the ready line when the steps show an iPhone that was connected and ready already, before any other was plugged in.

addPhoneIPhoneDetail: Pinky sets the iPhone up for you. Each step says what to do on the iPhone.

@addPhoneIPhoneDetail.description: Add phone › iPhone: the line under the title, above the steps.

addPhoneIPhoneDevModeWiFiNote: Don't see Developer Mode in Privacy & Security? Plug {name} in once: Pinky can make the switch appear only over the cable.

@addPhoneIPhoneDevModeWiFiNote.description: Add phone › iPhone and the checkup: under the Developer Mode step of a phone on Wi-Fi. name is its name.

addPhoneIPhoneFoundDetail: Pinky leaves these alone until you say they're yours. If one is yours, choose Use: Pinky sets it up over Wi-Fi, no cable needed.

@addPhoneIPhoneFoundTitle.description: Add phone › iPhone: above the steps, the iPhones and iPads Pinky found on Wi-Fi and has not used, each with Use and Ignore.

addPhoneIPhoneGetXcode: Get Xcode in the App Store

@addPhoneIPhoneGetXcode.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when this computer has no developer disk image (Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services; it comes with Xcode): the link that opens Xcode's page in the Mac App Store.

addPhoneIPhoneMirrorDetail: {source} keeps copies of Apple's files; the author of pymobiledevice3 runs it, not Apple. Pinky downloads the image from {image}, {size}, and checks every file against the checksum it expects.

@addPhoneIPhoneMirrorDetail.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when the computer has no developer disk image, below the official ways to get it: the offer to download it from a third-party mirror instead. What it is. source is the mirror's address, image which Xcode the image is from, size its size.

addPhoneIPhoneMirrorDone: Downloaded. Pinky is preparing the iPhone…

@addPhoneIPhoneMirrorDone.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when the computer has no developer disk image, below the official ways to get it: the offer to download it from a third-party mirror instead. Next to a spinner once the download is done, until the step moves on.

@addPhoneIPhoneMirrorDownload.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when the computer has no developer disk image, below the official ways to get it: the offer to download it from a third-party mirror instead. The button that starts the download. size is its size.

@addPhoneIPhoneMirrorDownloading.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when the computer has no developer disk image, below the official ways to get it: the offer to download it from a third-party mirror instead. Next to a spinner while it downloads.

@addPhoneIPhoneMirrorFailed.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when the computer has no developer disk image, below the official ways to get it: the offer to download it from a third-party mirror instead. When the download failed; Pinky's own reason follows in English.

addPhoneIPhoneMirrorMismatch: The mirror's files are not the ones Pinky expects, so Pinky did not use them.

@addPhoneIPhoneMirrorMismatch.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when the computer has no developer disk image, below the official ways to get it: the offer to download it from a third-party mirror instead. When a downloaded file's checksum differed from the one Pinky expects.

addPhoneIPhoneMirrorOfficial: You can still use an official copy instead, as described above.

@addPhoneIPhoneMirrorOfficial.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when the computer has no developer disk image, below the official ways to get it: the offer to download it from a third-party mirror instead. Under a failed download: the official ways above still work.

addPhoneIPhoneMirrorTitle: Or download it from a third-party mirror

@addPhoneIPhoneMirrorTitle.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when the computer has no developer disk image, below the official ways to get it: the offer to download it from a third-party mirror instead. Its title.

addPhoneIPhoneNoAnswer: {name} does not answer. Unplug it and plug it in again.

@addPhoneIPhoneNoAnswer.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the plug-in step when the iPhone is connected but does not answer; Pinky's own reason follows in English. name is the iPhone's name.

addPhoneIPhoneNoImageCopy: Apple's developer disk image comes with Xcode, which runs only on a Mac. On a Mac where Xcode was opened once, copy the folder /Library/Developer/DeveloperDiskImages/iOS_DDI into the folder named below.

@addPhoneIPhoneNoImageCopy.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when this computer has no developer disk image (Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services; it comes with Xcode): the text on Windows and Linux; Pinky's sentence with its folder follows. The path stays as it is.

addPhoneIPhoneNoImageMac: Apple's developer disk image comes with Xcode. Install Xcode from the App Store and open it once, then you can quit it: Pinky uses the image from then on.

@addPhoneIPhoneNoImageMac.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when this computer has no developer disk image (Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services; it comes with Xcode): the text on a Mac.

addPhoneIPhoneNoImageTitle: This computer has no developer disk image yet

@addPhoneIPhoneNoImageTitle.description: Add phone › iPhone, under the preparation step when this computer has no developer disk image (Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services; it comes with Xcode): the title of the box.

addPhoneIPhoneRefusedFolder: Pinky used the developer disk image in {folder}: build {build}, version {version}. Apple's signing server no longer signs it, so it can't be mounted on this iPhone. Replace it with the iOS_DDI folder of a Mac where the latest Xcode from the App Store was opened once.

@addPhoneIPhoneRefusedFolder.description: Add phone › iPhone and the phone's checkup, under the preparation step when Apple's signing server refused to sign the developer disk image Pinky found on this computer (Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services; it comes with Xcode), as Apple does with images it no longer signs, such as those of Xcode before 27: the text when the image is one the person put in a folder (Pinky's own, or the one the PINKY_DDI environment variable names); for Pinky's own folder, the offer to download an image from a third-party mirror instead (addPhoneIPhoneMirrorTitle) comes below it. folder is that folder; build is the Xcode build the image came with; version is the image's version, or a dash when unknown. iOS_DDI is a folder name.

addPhoneIPhoneRefusedMirror: Pinky used the developer disk image downloaded from the third-party mirror: build {build}, version {version}. Apple's signing server no longer signs it, so it can't be mounted on this iPhone. Install or update Xcode from the App Store and open it once, then you can quit it; or update Pinky once a version with a newer image is out.

@addPhoneIPhoneRefusedMirror.description: Add phone › iPhone and the phone's checkup, under the preparation step when Apple's signing server refused to sign the developer disk image Pinky found on this computer (Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services; it comes with Xcode), as Apple does with images it no longer signs, such as those of Xcode before 27: the text when the image was downloaded from the third-party mirror (addPhoneIPhoneMirrorTitle). build is the Xcode build the image came with; version is the image's version, or a dash when unknown.

addPhoneIPhoneRefusedRetry: Pinky tries again by itself as soon as another image is on this computer.

@addPhoneIPhoneRefusedRetry.description: Add phone › iPhone and the phone's checkup, under the preparation step when Apple's signing server refused to sign the developer disk image Pinky found on this computer (Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services; it comes with Xcode), as Apple does with images it no longer signs, such as those of Xcode before 27: a small note under the box.

addPhoneIPhoneRefusedTitle: Apple won't sign this developer disk image

@addPhoneIPhoneRefusedTitle.description: Add phone › iPhone and the phone's checkup, under the preparation step when Apple's signing server refused to sign the developer disk image Pinky found on this computer (Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services; it comes with Xcode), as Apple does with images it no longer signs, such as those of Xcode before 27: the title of the box.

addPhoneIPhoneRefusedXcode: Pinky used the developer disk image that Xcode installed on this Mac: build {build}, version {version}. Apple's signing server no longer signs it, so it can't be mounted on this iPhone. Install or update Xcode from the App Store and open it once: it installs a newer image, and you can quit it then.

@addPhoneIPhoneRefusedXcode.description: Add phone › iPhone and the phone's checkup, under the preparation step when Apple's signing server refused to sign the developer disk image Pinky found on this computer (Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services; it comes with Xcode), as Apple does with images it no longer signs, such as those of Xcode before 27: the text when the image came with Xcode on this Mac; below it come the App Store link (addPhoneIPhoneGetXcode) and the offer to download an image from a third-party mirror instead (addPhoneIPhoneMirrorTitle). build is the Xcode build the image came with; version is the image's version, or a dash when unknown.

@addPhoneIPhoneRetrying.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: a small note under a failed preparation step.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepDevMode.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: the step of turning on the iPhone's Developer Mode. Developer Mode is the iPhone's own name for the setting; use the name iOS shows in your language.

addPhoneIPhoneStepDevModeDetail: On the iPhone, open Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode, turn it on and tap Restart. After the restart, unlock the iPhone, tap Turn On and enter its passcode.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepDevModeDetail.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the Developer Mode step. Settings, Privacy & Security, Developer Mode, Restart and Turn On are the iPhone's own words; use the words iOS shows in your language.

addPhoneIPhoneStepDevModeNote: Pinky has made the Developer Mode switch appear; it is near the bottom of Privacy & Security.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepDevModeNote.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: a small note under the Developer Mode step: iOS hides the switch until a developer tool asks for it, and Pinky did.

addPhoneIPhoneStepDevModeWiFi: Done on the iPhone; if the switch isn't there, plug it in once

@addPhoneIPhoneStepDevModeWiFi.description: Add phone › iPhone: under the Developer Mode step's title while Pinky uses iPhones over Wi-Fi: the person turns it on, on the phone, over Wi-Fi too, but only a cable lets Pinky make the hidden switch appear.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepDriver.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: the first step on Windows, while Apple's driver (which comes with the Apple Devices app or iTunes) is missing.

addPhoneIPhoneStepDriverDetail: Install Apple Devices from the Microsoft Store, or iTunes from apple.com. Pinky talks to the iPhone through it.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepDriverDetail.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the Windows driver step. Apple Devices is the name of Apple's app in the Microsoft Store (in Chinese stores “Apple 设备”).

addPhoneIPhoneStepDriverWaiting: Waiting for it to be installed…

@addPhoneIPhoneStepDriverWaiting.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: next to a spinner under the driver or usbmuxd step: Pinky notices by itself once it is installed.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepPasscode.description: Add phone › iPhone, the phone's page and the checkup: the title of the step where the iPhone asks for its passcode before the WebDriverAgent helper may control it, as iOS does now and then.

addPhoneIPhoneStepPasscodeDetail: Enter the passcode on the iPhone: iOS asks for it now and then before the WebDriverAgent helper can control the phone. If the iPhone no longer asks, Pinky tries again in a few minutes, or at once when you plug it in again.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepPasscodeDetail.description: Add phone › iPhone, the phone's page and the checkup: what to do while the iPhone asks for its passcode before the WebDriverAgent helper may control it. WebDriverAgent is a name. Pinky starts the helper again later when nobody entered the passcode.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepPlug.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: the step of connecting the iPhone with a cable.

addPhoneIPhoneStepPlugDetail: Connect it to this computer with a USB cable, and unlock it.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepPlugDetail.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the plug-in step.

addPhoneIPhoneStepPlugWiFi: Once it trusts this computer, Pinky turns on its Wi-Fi connection, as Finder's “Show this iPhone when on Wi-Fi” does, so it keeps working when you unplug it while it's on the same Wi-Fi. One already connected to this computer over Wi-Fi shows up here without the cable, and Pinky asks you first.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepPlugWiFi.description: Add phone › iPhone: a note under the plug-in step while Pinky uses iPhones over Wi-Fi.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepPrepare.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: the step Pinky does by itself: mounting Apple's developer disk image on the iPhone.

addPhoneIPhoneStepPrepareDetail: Pinky mounts Apple's developer disk image on the iPhone, which takes a few seconds. iPhones on iOS 27 keep it when they restart; older ones drop it, and Pinky mounts it again by itself.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepPrepareDetail.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the preparation step. The developer disk image is Apple's add-on that gives a phone its developer services.

addPhoneIPhoneStepPrepareWiFi: Also works over Wi-Fi, more slowly

@addPhoneIPhoneStepPrepareWiFi.description: Add phone › iPhone: under the title of the step where Pinky mounts the developer disk image, while Pinky uses iPhones over Wi-Fi.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepPreparing.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: next to a spinner while Pinky mounts the developer disk image.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepTrust.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: the step of tapping Trust on the iPhone's “Trust This Computer?” question.

addPhoneIPhoneStepTrustCable: This step needs the cable: an iPhone asks to trust a computer only while it's plugged in.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepTrustCable.description: Add phone › iPhone: a note under the trust step.

addPhoneIPhoneStepTrustDetail: When the iPhone asks “Trust This Computer?”, tap Trust and enter its passcode. If it does not ask, unlock it; if you tapped Don't Trust, unplug it and plug it in again.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepTrustDetail.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the Trust step. “Trust This Computer?”, Trust and Don't Trust are the iPhone's own words; use the words iOS shows in your language.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepTrustHint.description: Add phone › iPhone: under the trust step's title while Pinky uses iPhones over Wi-Fi: this step needs the iPhone plugged in.

addPhoneIPhoneStepTrustWaiting: Waiting for the iPhone to trust this computer…

@addPhoneIPhoneStepTrustWaiting.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: next to a spinner under the Trust step.

addPhoneIPhoneStepTrustWiFiOn: Then Pinky turns on its Wi-Fi connection, as Finder's “Show this iPhone when on Wi-Fi” does. Turning off Use iPhones and iPads over Wi-Fi leaves it on.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepTrustWiFiOn.description: Add phone › iPhone: a note under the trust step while Pinky uses iPhones over Wi-Fi: Pinky turns on the iPhone's Wi-Fi connection (lockdown's EnableWifiConnections, Finder's checkbox) once it trusts the computer.

addPhoneIPhoneStepUnlock: Unlock the iPhone so Pinky can finish.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepUnlock.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the preparation step when the iPhone must be unlocked first (after a restart, for example).

@addPhoneIPhoneStepUsbmuxd.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: the first step on Linux, while usbmuxd (the daemon every iPhone connection goes through) is missing.

addPhoneIPhoneStepUsbmuxdDetail: Install the usbmuxd package, for example with sudo apt install usbmuxd. Pinky talks to the iPhone through it; it starts by itself when an iPhone is plugged in.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepUsbmuxdDetail.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the Linux usbmuxd step. The command stays as it is.

@addPhoneIPhoneStepsLabel.description: Add phone › iPhone: the accessibility label of the step list.

addPhoneIPhoneStuck: Pinky could not finish this step.

@addPhoneIPhoneStuck.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the preparation step when it failed; Pinky's own reason follows in English.

addPhoneIPhoneTooOld: This iPhone runs iOS {version}. Pinky needs iOS 17.4 or later: update it in Settings › General › Software Update.

@addPhoneIPhoneTooOld.description: Add phone › iPhone: the text of the box shown when the iPhone's iOS is too old. version is its iOS version. Settings, General and Software Update are the iPhone's own words.

@addPhoneIPhoneTooOldTitle.description: Add phone › iPhone: the title of the box shown in place of the steps when the iPhone's iOS is too old. name is the iPhone's name.

addPhoneIPhoneTrustWiFi: {name} is on Wi-Fi, where it can't be asked to trust this computer. Plug it in with a cable, unlock it and tap Trust.

@addPhoneIPhoneTrustWiFi.description: Add phone › iPhone and the phone's page: an iPhone on Wi-Fi that no longer trusts this computer. name is its name.

addPhoneIPhoneUnlockWiFi: Unlock {name}: Pinky connects to it over Wi-Fi once it's unlocked.

@addPhoneIPhoneUnlockWiFi.description: Add phone › iPhone: the phone the steps follow is on Wi-Fi and locked. name is its name.

addPhoneIPhoneUsbmuxdStopped: Not showing up? usbmuxd is installed but not running. Plug the iPhone in again, or start it with sudo systemctl start usbmuxd.

@addPhoneIPhoneUsbmuxdStopped.description: Add phone › iPhone, the step list: under the plug-in step on Linux, when no iPhone showed up for a while and usbmuxd is installed but not running. The command stays as it is.

@addPhoneLabel.description: Add phone: the accessibility label of the wizard's card, which walks the person through adding a phone.

@addPhoneLooking.description: Add phone › Android: the status line, next to a spinner, while Pinky waits for a newly plugged-in phone.

@addPhoneLookingIPhone.description: Add phone › iPhone: the status line, next to a spinner, while Pinky waits for the iPhone.

addPhoneOlderDetail: Older iPhones work too. Pick how to connect.

@addPhoneOlderDetail.description: Add phone › older iPhone: the line under the heading "Pair your iPhone", above two ways to connect.

@addPhoneOlderHelper.description: Add phone › older iPhone: the first way to connect, by installing a helper app (WebDriverAgent) on the iPhone. Also its accessibility label.

addPhoneOlderHelperDetail: WebDriverAgent, signed with your Apple ID. With a free Apple ID it needs re-signing every 7 days; a paid developer account lasts a year.

@addPhoneOlderHelperDetail.description: Add phone › older iPhone: under "Install the Pinky helper", what the helper is and how long its signature lasts. WebDriverAgent is a name.

@addPhoneOlderIPhone.description: Add phone › iPhone: the quiet button to the right of Pair that switches to the ways of connecting an older iPhone.

@addPhoneOlderMirroring.description: Add phone › older iPhone: the second way to connect, through macOS's iPhone Mirroring (use Apple's Simplified Chinese name for it). Also its accessibility label.

addPhoneOlderMirroringDetail: Nothing to install, but Pinky can read the screen only as an image, so it is slower.

@addPhoneOlderMirroringDetail.description: Add phone › older iPhone: under "Use iPhone Mirroring", its drawback.

addPhoneOlderNotYet: This build can't set that up yet: the gateway's iOS backends for older iPhones come in M3.

@addPhoneOlderNotYet.description: Add phone › older iPhone: shown once the person picks a way to connect, as neither works in this build yet. M3 is a milestone of the project.

addPhoneOlderTitle: This iPhone needs one more step

@addPhoneOlderTitle.description: Add phone › older iPhone: the heading of the box with the two ways to connect an older iPhone.

addPhoneOlderUpdate: Or update to iOS 27 for the best experience.

@addPhoneOlderUpdate.description: Add phone › older iPhone: the line under the two ways to connect, before the person picks one.

@addPhoneOrWiFi.description: Add phone › Android: the link under the USB step that switches to pairing the phone over Wi-Fi instead.

@addPhoneReady.description: Add phone › iPhone: the status line once the iPhone is paired and ready, next to a green dot. name is the iPhone's name.

@addPhoneTryAgain.description: Add phone: the button that looks for the phone again after it needed setup, and that asks for a new QR code after pairing over Wi-Fi failed.

@agentGeneric.description: Names an agent whose name is unknown, inside a sentence: "Note for the agent".

@agentGenericStart.description: Names an agent whose name is unknown, at the start of a sentence or label: "The agent's screen".

@agentRequestAskedAt.description: Ends the detail of an agent's first-connection request: when it asked, as 03:51.

@awayDialogConfirm.description: The dialog's button that turns it on.

awayDialogDrop: The phone's connection drops for a moment while adb restarts.

@awayDialogDrop.description: The dialog: what happens as it turns on.

awayDialogExposure: The phone listens on every network it joins, not only Tailscale: on a café's Wi-Fi, another device there could ask to debug it. The phone then asks you; tap Cancel. Only computers it already trusts get in without asking, and only the way through Tailscale is encrypted.

@awayDialogTitle.description: The dialog before turning Use away from home on: its title.

awayDialogUntil: It lasts until the phone restarts. Turn it off here any time; once it's off, you can turn it on again only while the phone is near this computer.

@awayDialogUntil.description: The dialog: how long it lasts and how to turn it off.

awayDialogWhat: Pinky has the phone's adb listen on the network at port 5555, as adb tcpip does, and connects to it through Tailscale wherever the phone is.

@awayDialogWhat.description: The dialog: what turning it on does. adb tcpip is a command; keep it.

awayFailed: Couldn't change Use away from home for {name}: {error}

@awayFailed.description: When turning it on or off failed; error is in English.

@awayHowTo.description: Button by awayNoTailscaleHere, awayNoTailscalePhone and awayOtherTailnet: opens Add phone › Android › Tailscale.

awayKeepAwake: Keep this computer awake for phones away

@awayKeepAwake.description: Settings › Phones, under the phones: the switch's title.

awayKeepAwakeDesc: While a phone is connected through Tailscale, this computer doesn't sleep when idle, so agents can reach the phone. A MacBook still sleeps when you close its lid, unless it's plugged in with an external display.
awayNoTailscaleHere: Needs Tailscale on this computer, signed in.

@awayNoTailscaleHere.description: Under awayTitle when Tailscale does not run on this computer.

awayNoTailscalePhone: Tailscale isn't connected on {name}. Install it there, open it and sign in to the same account as on this computer.

@awayNoTailscalePhone.description: Under awayTitle when the phone has no Tailscale connection: Tailscale is not installed, signed out or off on it, or another VPN is on instead. awayOneVPN follows.

awayNotConnected: Connect {name} by cable or on this computer's Wi-Fi to set it up.

@awayNotConnected.description: Under awayTitle when the phone is not connected.

awayOffDesc: Reach {name} through Tailscale when it's away from this computer's network.

@awayOffDesc.description: Under awayTitle while it is off.

awayOnDesc: On. When {name} is away from this computer's network, Pinky reaches it through Tailscale at {addr}.

@awayOnDesc.description: Under awayTitle while it is on: addr is the phone's Tailscale address.

awayOneVPN: Android runs one VPN at a time: while another VPN or proxy app is on, Tailscale is off. Turn that one off, then turn Tailscale on.

@awayOneVPN.description: Under awayNoTailscalePhone, and under the phone's step of the Tailscale steps (tailnetPhoneSteps): why Tailscale can be off on a phone that has it.

awayOtherTailnet: {name}'s Tailscale is signed in to another tailnet than this computer's. Sign in to the same account on both.

@awayOtherTailnet.description: Under awayTitle when the phone's Tailscale is connected, but to another tailnet (another account) than this computer's.

awayStoppedDesc: {name}'s adb stopped listening on the network, as it does when the phone restarts. Turn it on again before you leave.

@awayStoppedDesc.description: Under awayTitle while it is on but the phone's adb no longer listens.

@awayTitle.description: Settings › Phones, per Android phone: the title of the setting that reaches the phone through Tailscale when it is away from this computer's network.

@awayTurnOff.description: Button: turns Use away from home off.

@awayTurnOn.description: Button: opens the dialog that turns Use away from home on.

awayTurnedOff: Use away from home is off for {name}

@awayTurnedOff.description: A toast once Use away from home is off.

awayTurnedOn: {name} can now be used away from home

@awayTurnedOn.description: A toast once Use away from home is on.

@backgroundChangeFailed.description: A toast when turning Work in the background on or off failed. phone is the phone's name, reason the error in English.

backgroundDesc: Agents use a hidden second screen, so the phone stays yours and can stay locked. Applies from the next task.

@backgroundDesc.description: Settings › Phones: the line under Work in the background.

@backgroundTitle.description: Settings › Phones: a phone's switch (Android) that lets agents work on a hidden second display while the phone's own screen stays the person's.

backgroundUnsupported: {phone} can't work in the background yet.

@backgroundUnsupported.description: A toast when the phone cannot work in the background. phone is the phone's name.

@brandHonor.description: Add phone › Android: the choice of HONOR phones in the row of brands.

@brandHuawei.description: Add phone › Android: the choice of HUAWEI phones in the row of brands.

@brandOppo.description: Add phone › Android: the choice of OPPO, OnePlus and realme phones in the row of brands.

@brandOther.description: Add phone › Android: the choice of other Android phones in the row of brands.

@brandPixel.description: Add phone › Android: the choice of Google Pixel phones in the row of brands.

@brandSamsung.description: Add phone › Android: the choice of Samsung phones in the row of brands.

@brandVivo.description: Add phone › Android: the choice of vivo and iQOO phones in the row of brands.

@brandXiaomi.description: Add phone › Android: the choice of Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones in the row of brands.

@callAnswer.description: Inside toastCouldNot: the person's answer to an approval did not reach the gateway.

@callHandBack.description: Inside toastCouldNot: handing a phone back to the agent failed.

@callStop.description: Inside toastCouldNot: stopping a task failed.

@callTakeBackAlways.description: A verb phrase inside toastCouldNot, when Settings › Safety could not take back an Always allow answer.

@callTakeOver.description: Inside toastCouldNot: taking over a phone failed.

checkADBFail: Pinky can't reach adb, the Android tools it talks to phones through.
checkADBPass: Pinky talks to the phone through adb.

@checkADBTitle.description: The checkup: the item for adb, the tool Pinky talks to Android phones through.

checkAuthorizedAndroidFail: The phone hasn't allowed this computer yet. Unlock it, and when it asks “Allow USB debugging?”, tick “Always allow from this computer” and tap Allow.

@checkAuthorizedAndroidFail.description: The checkup, debugging allowed: an Android phone that has not allowed this computer. The quoted words are those of Android's prompt: use the words of Android's Simplified Chinese prompt.

checkAuthorizedFail: The phone hasn't allowed this computer yet.

@checkAuthorizedFail.description: The checkup, debugging allowed: failed, on a phone the system says no more of.

checkAuthorizedSkip: Checked once the phone is connected.

@checkAuthorizedSkip.description: The checkup, debugging allowed: not checked while the phone is not connected.

@checkAuthorizedTitle.description: The checkup: the item for whether the phone allows this computer.

checkBackgroundFail: Agents can't work on a hidden second screen on this phone.

@checkBackgroundFail.description: The checkup, working in the background: failed.

checkBackgroundOld: Needs Android 11 or later (this phone has Android {version}): agents use the phone's own screen.

@checkBackgroundOld.description: The checkup, working in the background: not on Android 10.

checkBackgroundPass: Agents can work on a hidden second screen while the phone stays off and locked.

@checkBackgroundPass.description: The checkup, working in the background: passed.

@checkBackgroundTitle.description: The checkup: the item for agents working on a hidden second screen.

checkBackgroundUnlocked: Before Android 13, agents can work on a second screen only while the phone is unlocked.

@checkBackgroundUnlocked.description: The checkup, working in the background: works on Android 11 and 12, only while the phone is unlocked.

checkCompanionMissing: Not installed. With it, Pinky reads the screen in about 70 ms instead of 2 s, and types any language without the clipboard.

@checkCompanionMissing.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion: not installed; an Install button follows.

checkCompanionNone: Pinky couldn't tell whether its companion app is installed.

@checkCompanionNone.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion: the check failed.

checkCompanionOff: Installed, but Pinky couldn't turn on its accessibility service.

@checkCompanionOff.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion: its service did not come on the last time Pinky tried; a Turn on button follows.

checkCompanionOffHuawei: If it keeps turning off: search Settings for App launch, turn off Manage automatically for Pinky Companion, and allow it to run in the background.

@checkCompanionOffHuawei.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion, on a HUAWEI or HONOR phone whose app's service is off. App launch and Manage automatically are Huawei's names: use those of its Simplified Chinese settings.

checkCompanionOffOppo: If it keeps turning off: in Developer options, turn on Disable permission monitoring; in the app's battery settings, allow background activity.

@checkCompanionOffOppo.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion, on an OPPO, OnePlus or realme phone whose app's service is off. Use ColorOS's Simplified Chinese names.

checkCompanionOffOther: If it keeps turning off: on Android 13 and later, open Settings › Apps › Pinky Companion, tap ⋮ › Allow restricted settings, then turn it on again.

@checkCompanionOffOther.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion, on other phones whose app's service is off. Allow restricted settings is Android's own name: use that of Android's Simplified Chinese settings.

checkCompanionOffVivo: If it keeps turning off: in Settings › Battery › Background power consumption management, choose Pinky Companion and don't restrict it, and allow it to start by itself.

@checkCompanionOffVivo.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion, on a vivo phone whose app's service is off: vivo turns off the service of apps that are not from its store. The Chinese menu names could not be confirmed, so they are described rather than quoted.

checkCompanionOffXiaomi: If it keeps turning off: in the app's settings, turn on Autostart and set Battery saver to No restrictions.

@checkCompanionOffXiaomi.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion, on a Xiaomi phone whose app's service is off: Xiaomi's cleaners stop apps, which turns their service off. Autostart and Battery saver are Xiaomi's names: use those of its Simplified Chinese settings.

checkCompanionOutdated: An older version is installed; Pinky carries a newer one.

@checkCompanionOutdated.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion: outdated; an Update button follows.

checkCompanionPass: Installed. Pinky turns it on only while an agent works on the phone, then reads the screen quickly and types any language.

@checkCompanionPass.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion: passed. Pinky turns the app's accessibility service on only while an agent works on the phone, and off again afterwards.

checkCompanionPublicKey: Installed, but signed with an old key that is public; Pinky carries the version signed with its private key.

@checkCompanionPublicKey.description: The checkup, Pinky Companion: the installed app is signed with the key of the builds until 8 November 2026, which was public, so anyone could make a fake update of it; an Update button follows.

@checkCompanionTitle.description: The checkup: the item for Pinky's companion app on the phone. Pinky Companion is the app's name: keep it as it is.

@checkConnectionAndroidFail.description: The checkup, connection: an Android phone that is not connected; steps follow.

checkConnectionAndroidNote: Over Wi-Fi: up to Android 16, Wireless debugging turns off when the phone leaves the Wi-Fi network (even for another access point of it) or restarts. Turn it on again, or pair again from Add phone.

@checkConnectionAndroidNote.description: The checkup, connection: a note for phones used over Wi-Fi. Wireless debugging is Android's own name.

checkConnectionAndroidStepCable: Plug it in with a USB cable that carries data, and unlock it.

@checkConnectionAndroidStepCable.description: The checkup, connection: the first step for an Android phone that is not connected.

checkConnectionAndroidStepDebugging: Check that USB debugging is still on, in Developer options:

@checkConnectionAndroidStepDebugging.description: The checkup, connection: the second step, above the menu path to Developer options.

@checkConnectionFail.description: The checkup, connection: a phone that is not connected.

@checkConnectionTailscale.description: The checkup, connection: passed, through Tailscale (the phone is away from this computer's network).

@checkConnectionTitle.description: The checkup: the item for whether the phone is connected.

@checkConnectionUSB.description: The checkup, connection: passed, over a USB cable.

@checkConnectionWiFi.description: The checkup, connection and Wi-Fi: passed, over Wi-Fi.

@checkDeveloperModePass.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: Developer Mode is on.

@checkDeveloperModeTitle.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the title of the Developer Mode item. Developer Mode is the iPhone's own name for the setting; use the name iOS shows in your language.

checkDiskImageDownloadNote: Show the steps to download it from a third-party mirror instead.

@checkDiskImageDownloadNote.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: a note under the item when this computer has no developer disk image: Add phone's steps (the button below) offer a download from a third-party mirror.

checkDiskImageRefusedNote: Show the steps to download an image from a third-party mirror instead. Pinky tries again by itself as soon as another image is on this computer.

@checkDiskImageRefusedNote.description: The phone's checkup, under the developer disk image item when Apple's signing server refused to sign the image that came with Xcode on this Mac (addPhoneIPhoneRefusedXcode) or one the person put in Pinky's folder (addPhoneIPhoneRefusedFolder): a note saying that the setup steps (the button phoneSetUpIPhone) also offer to download an image from a third-party mirror (addPhoneIPhoneMirrorTitle), and that Pinky tries again once another image is there. Say it as checkDiskImageDownloadNote does.

checkDiskImageMissing: Not mounted, so the iPhone doesn't offer what Pinky needs.

@checkDiskImageMissing.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the image is not mounted; Pinky's reason follows in English.

checkDiskImageNoCopy: Mounted, but this computer has no copy of it, so Pinky can't mount it again should it go missing (iPhones below iOS 27 drop it when they restart).

@checkDiskImageNoCopy.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the image is mounted, but this computer has none to mount again should it go missing; the steps below say where to get one.

checkDiskImagePass: Mounted. Should it go missing (iPhones below iOS 27 drop it when they restart), Pinky mounts it again by itself.

@checkDiskImagePass.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the image is mounted, and this computer has one to mount again should it go missing.

@checkDiskImageTitle.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the title of the item about Apple's developer disk image, the add-on that gives the iPhone its developer services.

checkHelperExpired: The helper on {phone} stopped working on {when, date, ::MMMMEEEEdjmm}: its signature ran out. Install it again from Xcode; signed with a free Apple ID, it lasts 7 days.

@checkHelperExpired.description: Checkup and the Phone screen, an iPhone's helper (WebDriverAgent): the signature (provisioning profile) made with the person's Apple ID ran out, so the iPhone no longer starts the helper; the button below opens how to install it. phone is the iPhone's name; when is when it ran out, with the time.

@checkHelperHow.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the button that opens the instructions for installing the helper.

checkHelperMissing: WebDriverAgent isn't installed or doesn't answer. Below iOS 27 an iPhone takes taps and typing only through it; without it Pinky can only read the screen and open apps.

@checkHelperMissing.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the helper is missing or does not answer.

@checkHelperPass.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the helper answers.

checkHelperSoon: The helper on {phone} stops working on {when, date, ::MMMMEEEEdjmm}: install it again from Xcode.

@checkHelperSoon.description: Checkup and a reminder on the Phone screen, an iPhone's helper (WebDriverAgent): its signature (provisioning profile) runs out within two days, after which the iPhone no longer starts the helper; the button beside it opens how to install it. phone is the iPhone's name; when is when it runs out, with the time.

@checkHelperTitle.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the title of the item about the WebDriverAgent helper, the app Pinky drives iPhones below iOS 27 through.

checkHelperUntil: Its signature lasts until {when, date, ::yMMMMd}. Pinky reminds you two days before.

@checkHelperUntil.description: Checkup, an iPhone's helper (WebDriverAgent) that works: a note on when its signature (provisioning profile) runs out. when is that day, with the year.

checkHostADBOld: The adb server running on this computer is too old to pair phones over Wi-Fi. Quit the program that started it, such as an old Android SDK's tools, or update them: Pinky then starts its own.

@checkHostADBOld.description: The checkup and Add phone › Android: the adb server that runs is older than Wi-Fi pairing needs.

checkHostADBRestarts: Another program keeps replacing the adb server, so phones drop off now and then. It's usually a program with another version of adb: quit it, or have it use the same adb as Pinky.

@checkHostADBRestarts.description: The checkup and Add phone › Android: the adb server went away again and again, as when another program with another adb replaces it.

checkHostADBServer: Android's adb server isn't running, and Pinky couldn't start it.

@checkHostADBServer.description: The checkup and Add phone › Android: no adb server runs and starting one failed; the system's words follow.

checkHostNoADB: Pinky found no adb, the tool it talks to Android phones through. Install Android's SDK Platform-Tools, then open Pinky again.

@checkHostNoADB.description: The checkup and Add phone › Android: the computer has no adb at all (a build of Pinky without its own).

@checkHostTitle.description: The checkup: the item for software this computer needs for the phone's platform, on a phone that is not Android (Android's is checkADBTitle).

checkInputFail: Pinky couldn't send a key to the phone.

@checkInputFail.description: The checkup, tapping and typing: failed for another reason; the system's words follow.

checkInputIPhoneNoHelper: No taps or typing without the Pinky helper.

@checkInputIPhoneNoHelper.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the input item of an iPhone below iOS 27 without the helper.

checkInputIPhonePass: The iPhone's touch and key service answers.

@checkInputIPhonePass.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the input item passed: the phone's input service accepted a connection (Pinky sends no tap to check).

checkInputOppo: In Developer options, turn on “Disable permission monitoring”, then restart the phone.

@checkInputOppo.description: The checkup, tapping and typing, on an OPPO, OnePlus or realme phone. Disable permission monitoring is the name of ColorOS's switch: use the name of its Simplified Chinese settings.

checkInputOther: In Developer options, look for a switch that lets USB debugging simulate input, turn it on, then restart the phone.

@checkInputOther.description: The checkup, tapping and typing, on other phones.

@checkInputOtherNote.description: The checkup, tapping and typing, on other phones: under checkInputOther.

checkInputPass: Pinky can tap, swipe and type on the phone.

@checkInputPass.description: The checkup, tapping and typing: passed.

checkInputRefused: The phone refuses taps and keys from this computer.

@checkInputRefused.description: The checkup, tapping and typing: the phone refused the input; the maker's steps follow.

checkInputRestart: “USB debugging (Security settings)” is on, but takes effect only after a restart. Restart the phone, then check again.

@checkInputRestart.description: The checkup, tapping and typing, on a Xiaomi phone that has the switch on but was not restarted since. Use the name of Xiaomi's Simplified Chinese settings.

@checkInputTitle.description: The checkup: the item for whether taps and keys from the computer reach the phone.

checkInputXiaomi: In Developer options, turn on “USB debugging (Security settings)”, then restart the phone.

@checkInputXiaomi.description: The checkup, tapping and typing, on a Xiaomi phone. USB debugging (Security settings) is the name of Xiaomi's switch: use the name of Xiaomi's Simplified Chinese settings.

checkInputXiaomiNote: Turning it on checks with Xiaomi online: the phone needs a network, and may ask for a SIM card or your Xiaomi account.

@checkInputXiaomiNote.description: The checkup, tapping and typing, on a Xiaomi phone: what turning the switch on needs.

checkLocalNetworkFail: macOS doesn't let Pinky look for phones on your network, so pairing over Wi-Fi can't find the phone. Turn on Pinky under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network.

@checkLocalNetworkFail.description: The checkup, local network: failed; a button to open the setting follows. System Settings, Privacy & Security and Local Network are macOS's own names: use those of macOS in Simplified Chinese.

checkLocalNetworkNote: If macOS just asked whether Pinky may find devices on your local network, click Allow, then check again.

@checkLocalNetworkNote.description: The checkup, local network: under checkLocalNetworkFail.

checkLocalNetworkPass: Pinky may look for phones on this network, which pairing over Wi-Fi needs.

@checkLocalNetworkTitle.description: The checkup, on a Mac: the item for macOS letting Pinky look for phones on the network.

checkLocalNetworkUnknown: Pinky couldn't tell whether it may use the local network.

@checkLocalNetworkUnknown.description: The checkup, local network: the check could not run.

checkScreenFail: The phone sends no screenshots, so agents can't see the screen. Restart the phone, then check again.

@checkScreenFail.description: The checkup, seeing the screen: failed.

checkScreenNoVideo: The phone's video encoder doesn't work with Pinky, so the mirror shows still pictures. Agents still see the screen.

@checkScreenNoVideo.description: The checkup, seeing the screen: works without the live picture.

@checkScreenPass.description: The checkup, seeing the screen: passed.

@checkScreenTitle.description: The checkup: the item for screenshots and the live picture.

@checkTrustedPass.description: Checkup, an iPhone's item: the iPhone trusts this computer (its answer to "Trust This Computer?"). The item's title is Add phone's "Trust this computer".

checkUSBNotReady: This computer can't use the phone over USB yet.

@checkUSBNotReady.description: The checkup and Add phone: an Android phone listed as needing setup on macOS or Windows (on Windows: its USB debugging has no driver); the system's words follow.

checkUSBPermission: This computer isn't allowed to open the phone's USB connection.

@checkUSBPermission.description: The checkup and Add phone: an Android phone the computer may not open (Linux without udev rules).

checkUSBPermissionNote: On Linux: add yourself to the plugdev group (sudo usermod -aG plugdev $LOGNAME), log out and in again, and install your distribution's udev rules for Android phones (android-sdk-platform-tools-common on Ubuntu and Debian). Then unplug the phone and plug it in again.

@checkUSBPermissionNote.description: The checkup and Add phone: how to fix checkUSBPermission. android-udev-rules and plugdev are names of Linux packages and groups: keep them as they are.

checkWiFiFail: Pinky can't use this phone over Wi-Fi.
checkWiFiIPhoneFail: Pinky couldn't turn on its Wi-Fi connection. Plug it in again to try once more, or tick “Show this iPhone when on Wi-Fi” in Finder.

@checkWiFiIPhoneFail.description: An iPhone's or iPad's checkup, the Wi-Fi item: Pinky could not turn on the phone's Wi-Fi connection (lockdown's EnableWifiConnections, Finder's checkbox); the error shows under it.

checkWiFiIPhoneNotSeen: Its Wi-Fi connection is on, but this computer doesn't see it on Wi-Fi. Check that both are on the same Wi-Fi network: guest networks and some routers keep devices apart, and a VPN on either can hide it. A phone whose Wi-Fi connection was just turned on can take a minute to show up.

@checkWiFiIPhoneNotSeen.description: An iPhone's or iPad's checkup, the Wi-Fi item: the phone's Wi-Fi connection is on, but the computer's device service does not list it over the network.

checkWiFiIPhoneOff: Use iPhones and iPads over Wi-Fi is off in Settings › Phones, so Pinky leaves its Wi-Fi connection as it is.

@checkWiFiIPhoneOff.description: An iPhone's or iPad's checkup, the Wi-Fi item: Pinky's Wi-Fi setting is off, so it did not look at the phone's Wi-Fi connection.

checkWiFiIPhoneSeen: Its Wi-Fi connection is on, and this computer sees it on Wi-Fi: unplugged, it keeps working while it's on the same Wi-Fi.

@checkWiFiIPhoneSeen.description: An iPhone's or iPad's checkup, the Wi-Fi item, while the phone is on its cable and also listed over the network.

checkWiFiIPhoneTurnedOn: Pinky turned it on when you plugged it in, as Finder's “Show this iPhone when on Wi-Fi” does.

@checkWiFiIPhoneTurnedOn.description: An iPhone's or iPad's checkup, a note under the Wi-Fi item: Pinky turned on the phone's Wi-Fi connection itself.

checkWiFiIPhoneUnknown: Pinky turns on its Wi-Fi connection once it's plugged in and trusts this computer.

@checkWiFiIPhoneUnknown.description: An iPhone's or iPad's checkup, the Wi-Fi item, before Pinky could look at the phone's Wi-Fi connection (not plugged in since Pinky started, or not trusting the computer yet).

checkWiFiOld: Pairing over Wi-Fi needs Android 11 or later (this phone has Android {version}). Use USB.

@checkWiFiOld.description: The checkup, Wi-Fi: not on Android 10.

checkWiFiPass: You can also pair this phone over Wi-Fi, from Add phone.

@checkWiFiPass.description: The checkup, Wi-Fi: the phone can be paired over Wi-Fi.

@checkWiFiTitle.description: The checkup: the item for using the phone over Wi-Fi.

@checkupAgain.description: The checkup: the button that runs it again.

@checkupAllGood.description: The checkup: the summary line when every item passed.

@checkupBack.description: The checkup page: the button that shows the phone's screen again.

@checkupFailLabel.description: The checkup: the accessible name of an item's cross.

@checkupFailed.description: The checkup: when it could not run. error is the system's reason, in English.

@checkupFor.description: The checkup page's heading: Pinky checks what it needs on the phone, item by item.

checkupIntro: Pinky checks what it needs on the phone and on this computer, item by item, and says what to do about anything that doesn't work.

@checkupIntro.description: The checkup page: the line under its heading.

@checkupPassLabel.description: The checkup: the accessible name of an item's check mark.

@checkupRunning.description: The checkup: next to a spinner while it runs.

@checkupSkipLabel.description: The checkup: the accessible name of an item's dash.

@checkupSystem.description: The checkup: the system the phone runs, as Pinky read it.

checkupTimeout: the phone took too long to answer

@checkupTimeout.description: The checkup: the reason in checkupFailed when the phone did not answer in time.

checkupToFix: {count, plural, one {# item to fix} other {# items to fix}}

@checkupToFix.description: The checkup: the summary line when items failed.

checkupUnsupported: This version of Pinky can't run checkups.

@checkupUnsupported.description: The checkup, with a gateway that cannot run one.

checkupWaitOnline: The other checks run once the phone is connected.

@checkupWaitOnline.description: The checkup of a phone that is not connected or not allowed yet.

@checkupWarnLabel.description: The checkup: the accessible name of an item's warning mark.

companionAllowHint: If the phone asks, allow the install.

@companionAllowHint.description: The Pinky Companion card: under the progress bar while the app installs, and in small type under the buttons before.

companionAllowHintOppo: If the phone shows a permission notice, tap Continue installing; some phones ask for your OPPO account.

@companionAllowHintOppo.description: The Pinky Companion card and the checkup, on an OPPO, OnePlus or realme phone, while Pinky installs the app: what to do on the phone. Continue installing is the button of ColorOS's page: use its Simplified Chinese name.

companionAllowHintXiaomi: On the phone, tap Install within 10 seconds; keep it unlocked.

@companionAllowHintXiaomi.description: The Pinky Companion card and the checkup, on a Xiaomi phone, while Pinky installs the app: what to do on the phone. Install is the button of Xiaomi's prompt: use its Simplified Chinese name.

@companionCardLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Pinky Companion card. name is the phone's name.

companionErrDeclined: The install was declined on the phone. Try again, and tap Install when the phone asks.

@companionErrDeclined.description: The Pinky Companion card and the checkup: the error when the person or the phone declined the install (the phone's own confirmation).

companionErrOffline: The phone went offline. Connect it again, then try again.

@companionErrOffline.description: The Pinky Companion card: the error when the phone went offline during the install.

@companionErrOther.description: The Pinky Companion card: the error when the install failed for another reason. detail is the error, in English.

companionErrPlayProtect: Google Play Protect stopped the install. On the phone, choose Install anyway, then try again.

@companionErrPlayProtect.description: The Pinky Companion card: the error when Google Play Protect stopped the install. Install anyway is the button of Play Protect's prompt.

companionErrRestricted: The phone blocked installing apps over USB. If it asked you to confirm, tap Install; if Developer options has a switch such as Install via USB, turn it on. Then try again.

@companionErrRestricted.description: The Pinky Companion card and the checkup: the error when the phone blocked installs over USB, on a phone whose maker Pinky does not know.

companionErrRestrictedXiaomi: The phone blocked the install. In Developer options, turn on Install via USB (it needs your Xiaomi account), then try again with the phone unlocked, and tap Install on it within 10 seconds.

@companionErrRestrictedXiaomi.description: The Pinky Companion card and the checkup, on a Xiaomi phone: the error when the phone blocked installs over USB (the switch is off, or nobody tapped Install in time). Install via USB and Install are Xiaomi's names: use those of its Simplified Chinese settings.

companionErrSettings: The phone refuses to let the computer turn on the app's accessibility service: {detail}

@companionErrSettings.description: The Pinky Companion card and the checkup: turning on the app's service failed because the phone refuses settings changes from the computer, on a phone whose maker Pinky does not know.

detail.example: Permission denial: writing to settings requires WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

companionErrSettingsOppo: The phone refuses to let the computer turn on the app. In Developer options, turn on Disable permission monitoring, restart the phone, then try again.

@companionErrSettingsOppo.description: The Pinky Companion card and the checkup, on an OPPO, OnePlus or realme phone: turning on the app's service failed because permission monitoring is on. Use ColorOS's Simplified Chinese name for the switch.

companionErrSettingsXiaomi: The phone refuses to let the computer turn on the app. In Developer options, turn on USB debugging (Security settings), restart the phone, then try again.

@companionErrSettingsXiaomi.description: The Pinky Companion card and the checkup, on a Xiaomi phone: turning on the app's service failed because USB debugging (Security settings) is off. Use the name of Xiaomi's Simplified Chinese settings.

companionErrStorage: The phone is out of space. Free some up, then try again.

@companionErrStorage.description: The Pinky Companion card: the error when the phone has no room for the app.

companionErrTimeout: The install didn't finish. If the phone asked to allow it, tap Allow there, then try again.

@companionErrTimeout.description: The Pinky Companion card: the error when the install did not finish in time. Allow is the button of the phone's install prompt.

@companionInstall.description: The Pinky Companion card: the button that installs the app on the phone.

companionInstallBody: A small Pinky app for {name}. Agents control the phone faster and more steadily with it, and type without using its clipboard. Pinky turns it on only while an agent works.

@companionInstallBody.description: The Pinky Companion card, when the app is not installed: why to install it. Pinky turns its accessibility service on only while an agent works on the phone. name is the phone's name. The card is in a narrow side panel.

@companionInstallLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Install button of the Pinky Companion card. name is the phone's name.

@companionInstallTitle.description: The title of the card on an Android phone's side panel that offers to install Pinky Companion, Pinky's app for the phone.

@companionInstalling.description: The Pinky Companion card: the accessibility label of the progress bar while the app installs.

@companionInstallingTitle.description: The Pinky Companion card's title while Pinky installs or updates the app.

@companionLineMissing.description: Settings › Phones: a phone's line about Pinky Companion when the app is not on the phone.

companionLineNoAPK: This Pinky has no companion app to install

@companionLineNoAPK.description: Settings › Phones: a phone's line about Pinky Companion when this build of Pinky does not include the app.

companionLineOff: Pinky couldn't turn on Pinky Companion

@companionLineOff.description: Settings › Phones: a phone's line about Pinky Companion when its service did not come on the last time Pinky tried.

@companionLineOn.description: Settings › Phones: a phone's line about Pinky Companion, Pinky's app for the phone, while its accessibility service is on: an agent works on the phone.

@companionLineOutdated.description: Settings › Phones: a phone's line about Pinky Companion when this Pinky comes with a newer version.

companionLinePublicKey: Pinky Companion has a security update

@companionLinePublicKey.description: Settings › Phones: a phone's line about Pinky Companion when the installed app is signed with the old public key and this Pinky carries the version signed with its private key.

companionLineReady: Pinky Companion turns on only while an agent works

@companionLineReady.description: Settings › Phones: a phone's line about Pinky Companion, Pinky's app for the phone, when it is installed and ready: Pinky turns its accessibility service on only while an agent works on the phone, so that the phone's apps (banking apps check for such services) see it only then.

@companionNotNow.description: The Pinky Companion card: the quiet button that hides the card for this phone.

@companionOnToast.description: A notice after Pinky installed, updated or turned on Pinky Companion, its app for Android phones, and checked that its service comes on. It is on only while an agent works on the phone. name is the phone's name.

companionPublicKeyBody: Pinky Companion on this phone is signed with an old key that is public, so anyone could make a fake update of it. The new version is signed with Pinky's private key: once you update, it is safe.

@companionPublicKeyBody.description: The Pinky Companion card, when the installed app is signed with the key of the builds until 8 November 2026, which was public, and this Pinky carries the version signed with its private key: why to update soon. Shown in place of the usual update text, often on phones where the person has to click Update because the phone asks before installs over USB. Keep it plain, not alarming. The card is in a narrow side panel.

companionStillWaiting: Still waiting for the phone. Look for a prompt on its screen.

@companionStillWaiting.description: The Pinky Companion card: when the install has taken more than 20 seconds, as the phone may be asking to allow it.

@companionTurnOn.description: The Pinky Companion card: the button that turns the app's service on.

companionTurnOnBody: Pinky couldn't turn on the app's service the last time it tried, so agents control the phone the slower way. Try again to see why.

@companionTurnOnBody.description: The Pinky Companion card, when the app's service did not come on the last time Pinky tried (some phones refuse settings changes from the computer): why to try again. Turn on, the button, shows the reason if it fails again.

@companionTurnOnLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Turn on button of the Pinky Companion card. name is the phone's name.

@companionTurnOnTitle.description: The title of the card that offers to turn on Pinky Companion's service when the app is installed but off.

@companionUpdate.description: The Pinky Companion card: the button that updates the app on the phone.

companionUpdateBody: This Pinky comes with a newer version of its app for the phone. Updating keeps control fast and steady.

@companionUpdateBody.description: The Pinky Companion card, when the phone has an older version: why to update it.

@companionUpdateLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Update button of the Pinky Companion card. name is the phone's name.

@companionUpdateTitle.description: The title of the card that offers to update Pinky Companion on the phone to the version this Pinky comes with.

companionUpdatingHint: Agents can use the phone again in a few seconds.

@companionUpdatingHint.description: Under the companion card's progress bar while it updates.

@companionUpdatingLabel.description: The accessibility label of the companion card's progress bar while it updates.

@companionUpdatingTitle.description: The companion card's title while Pinky updates the app by itself.

@connectAlsoWorks.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent, when no agent is installed: under the buttons, the other agents Pinky can connect. names is a list.

@connectByHand.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the link that shows the commands to add Pinky to an agent yourself.

@connectByHandHide.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the link that hides the commands again (connectByHand shows them).

@connectCardBroken.description: The title of the sidebar's card for an agent whose entry for Pinky starts something that does not work (connectWhyMissing or connectWhyCoreutils under it), and its accessibility label.

@connectCardChoose.description: The button on the sidebar's card when several agents are installed: it opens Settings › Agents to connect one.

connectCardFound: Pinky found {names} on this computer. Connect one to let it use your phones.

@connectCardFound.description: The sidebar's card while no agent is connected and several are installed. names is a list such as “Claude Code, Codex and Cursor”.

connectCardFoundOne: Pinky found {agent} on this computer. Connect it to let it use your phones.

@connectCardFoundOne.description: The sidebar's card while no agent is connected and one agent is installed, above the button that connects it.

@connectCardGet.description: The button on the sidebar's card when no agent is installed: it opens Settings › Agents, which links to where to get one.

@connectCardLater.description: The sidebar's card about connecting an agent: hides it until Pinky starts again.

connectCardNone: Pinky lets an AI agent use your phone. Install one, such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop, then connect it.

@connectCardNone.description: The sidebar's card while no agent is connected and none is installed. Keep the names Claude Code and Claude Desktop.

@connectClaudeHint.description: Settings › Agents › Add an agent: under the heading Claude Code, above the claude mcp add command that adds Pinky to Claude Code.

connectCommandLabel: Command that starts Pinky for an agent

@connectCommandLabel.description: Settings › Agents › Add an agent: the accessibility label of the command shown under Other agents.

@connectConnect.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the button on an agent's row that adds Pinky to the agent's settings.

@connectConnectLabel.description: The accessibility label of an agent's Connect button in Settings › Agents, and the text of the button on the sidebar's card when Pinky found one agent.

connectCopyClaude: Copy the command for Claude Code

@connectCopyClaude.description: Settings › Agents › Add an agent: the accessibility label of the copy button next to the claude mcp add command.

connectCopyOther: Copy the command for other agents

@connectCopyOther.description: Settings › Agents › Add an agent: the accessibility label of the copy button next to the command under Other agents.

connectDoneNow: Connected. Ask {agent} to do something on your phone.

@connectDoneNow.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: under an agent once Pinky is added, for an agent that reads the change at once.

connectDoneOpened: Pinky's extension is open in {agent}: click Install there.

@connectDoneOpened.description: Under Claude Desktop in Settings › Agents, and on the sidebar's card, after Connect opened Pinky's extension (.mcpb) in Claude Desktop, which asks the person to install it. Keep Install as Claude Desktop's button says it.

connectDoneRestart: Connected. Quit {agent} and open it again, then ask it to do something on your phone.

@connectDoneRestart.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: under an agent once Pinky is added, for an app that reads its settings when it opens (Claude).

connectDoneSession: Connected. Start a new {agent} session, then ask it to do something on your phone.

@connectDoneSession.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: under an agent once Pinky is added, for an agent that reads its MCP servers when a session starts (Claude Code, Codex).

@connectFailed.description: Under an agent in Settings › Agents, and on the sidebar's card, when connecting it or removing Pinky failed. error is Pinky's or the agent's own message, in English.

error.example: Pinky left ~/.cursor/mcp.json as it is: not valid JSON at byte 40

@connectFix.description: The button on the sidebar's card for an agent that can't start Pinky (connectCardBroken), which sets its entry right.

@connectFixLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Fix button on the sidebar's card.

@connectFoundLabel.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the accessibility label of the list of agents found on this computer.

@connectGet.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent, when no agent is installed: a button that opens the agent's download page.

connectIntro: Connect adds Pinky to an agent's settings on this computer, after keeping a copy of them. You allow each agent the first time it connects.

@connectIntro.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the line under the heading, above the agents found on this computer.

connectIntroByHand: Agents on this computer start Pinky with a command, and you allow each one the first time it connects.

@connectIntroByHand.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent, in a Pinky that cannot change agents' settings: the line under the heading, above the commands.

connectKeptCopy: Pinky kept a copy of the settings as they were.

@connectKeptCopy.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: under an agent after Pinky changed its settings file, before the Show link (connectShowCopy).

connectLooking: Looking for agents on this computer…

@connectLooking.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: in place of the list of agents while Pinky looks for them.

connectManual: Pinky can't change its settings here. Add it by hand.

@connectManual.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the second line of an agent that Pinky cannot connect on this system (Add an agent by hand below shows the commands).

connectNoneFound: Pinky found no agent on this computer. Install one, then connect it here.

@connectNoneFound.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: in place of the list when no agent Pinky knows is installed, above the buttons that open where to get one.

@connectNotHere.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: under the list, the agents Pinky knows how to connect that are not installed here. names is a list such as “Cursor, Windsurf and Gemini CLI”.

connectOtherHint: Set this as the command of an MCP server over stdio.

@connectOtherHint.description: Settings › Agents › Add an agent: under Other agents, above the command (Pinky's path and the argument mcp) that agents' MCP settings take. Keep MCP and stdio.

@connectOtherTitle.description: Settings › Agents › Add an agent: the heading above the command other agents (Codex, Cursor…) run to reach Pinky.

@connectProblem.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the second line of an agent whose settings file Pinky cannot read, such as one with a mistake in it. problem is the file and what is wrong with it, in English.

problem.example: ~/.cursor/mcp.json: not valid JSON at line 3, column 14: expected a colon

@connectRemove.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the button on a connected agent's row that takes Pinky out of its settings.

@connectRemoveLabel.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the accessibility label of an agent's Remove button.

connectRemoveTip: Takes Pinky out of {file}, after keeping a copy of it

@connectRemoveTip.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the tooltip of an agent's Remove button. file is the agent's settings file.

@connectRemoved.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: under an agent once Pinky is taken out of its settings.

connectRemovedRestart: Removed. {agent} stops using Pinky once you quit it and open it again.

@connectRemovedRestart.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: under an app that reads its settings when it opens, once Pinky is taken out of them.

@connectShowCopy.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the link after connectKeptCopy that shows the copy of the agent's settings in Finder or the file manager.

@connectShowCopyLabel.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the accessibility label of the Show link.

@connectShowFile.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: a link under an agent whose settings file Pinky cannot read (connectProblem), which shows the file in Finder or the file manager so the person can fix it.

@connectShowFileLabel.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the accessibility label of the Show the file link.

@connectStateConnected.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the second line of an agent whose settings start this Pinky.

connectStateExtension: Connected as an extension. Remove it in {agent}'s Settings › Extensions.

@connectStateExtension.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the second line of Claude Desktop when Pinky is installed as its extension (from Pinky's .mcpb), which only Claude Desktop removes. Keep Settings › Extensions as Claude Desktop names it.

@connectStateNotConnected.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the second line of an agent on this computer that does not have Pinky.

connectTip: Adds Pinky to {file}, after keeping a copy of it
