@connectTip.description: The tooltip of an agent's Connect, Update and Fix buttons, in Settings › Agents and on the sidebar's card. file is the agent's settings file.

connectTipOpens: Opens Pinky's extension in {agent}, which asks you to install it

@connectTipOpens.description: The tooltip of Claude Desktop's Connect button, in Settings › Agents and on the sidebar's card: Connect opens Pinky's extension (.mcpb) in Claude Desktop instead of changing a file.

@connectTitle.description: Settings › Agents: the heading of the part that connects the agents on this computer to Pinky (or, without that, says how to add one by hand), and its accessibility label; also the title of the sidebar's card that suggests connecting an agent while none is, and of the link under Tasks then.

@connectToastConnected.description: A toast once Pinky was added to an agent's settings.

@connectToastOpened.description: A toast once Connect opened Pinky's extension in Claude Desktop.

@connectUpdate.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the button on the row of an agent whose entry for Pinky is out of date (it starts a Pinky that moved, say), which sets it right.

@connectUpdateLabel.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the accessibility label of an agent's Update button.

connectWhyCoreutils: Starts “pinky”, which may be another program of that name

@connectWhyCoreutils.description: The second line of an agent set up with the old command pinky mcp, which many computers run as coreutils' own pinky, in Settings › Agents and on the sidebar's card. Keep “pinky” as it is.

connectWhyMissing: Starts a Pinky that is no longer there

@connectWhyMissing.description: The second line of an agent whose entry for Pinky starts a program that is gone (Pinky moved), in Settings › Agents and on the sidebar's card.

@connectWhyOff.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the second line of Claude Desktop when Pinky's extension is installed but turned off there.

@connectWhyOther.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the second line of an agent whose MCP server named pinky starts something else. command is that command line.

@connectWhyOtherPinky.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the second line of an agent whose entry starts Pinky from another place than the one open.

connectWhySkill: Connected, with an old copy of Pinky's guide

@connectWhySkill.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the second line of an agent that has Pinky, but whose copy of Pinky's skill (the guide agents read) is missing or from another version; Update installs the current one.

@connectWorking.description: Settings › Agents › Connect an agent: the accessibility label of the spinner on an agent's row while Pinky adds itself to the agent or removes itself.

@connectionAuto.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: the first choice, which goes by the iOS version.

connectionAutoDesc: Without the helper on iOS 27 and later; through the WebDriverAgent helper on older iPhones that have it.

@connectionAutoDesc.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: what Automatic does.

@connectionAutoNow.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: Automatic while it is chosen, with the way it picked. way is CoreDevice, WebDriverAgent, or the words of connectionReadOnly.

connectionChangeFailed: Couldn't change how Pinky connects to {phone}: {reason}

@connectionChangeFailed.description: A toast when choosing an iPhone's connection failed. phone is the phone's name, reason the error in English.

@connectionChoose.description: A link or button for an iPhone whose chosen connection does not work with it: opens Settings › Phones, where the connection is chosen.

connectionChosenNeedsIOS27: This iPhone is set to connect through CoreDevice, which needs iOS 27 or later; it runs iOS {version}. Choose Automatic or the WebDriverAgent helper in Settings › Phones.

@connectionChosenNeedsIOS27.description: The phone's page, its checkup and Add phone › iPhone, for an iPhone below iOS 27 whose connection in Settings › Phones was set to CoreDevice (connectionCoreDevice), which it cannot use. Automatic and the WebDriverAgent helper are the other choices there (connectionAuto, connectionWDA). CoreDevice and WebDriverAgent are names.

@connectionCoreDevice.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: the way through Xcode's CoreDevice protocol. CoreDevice is a name.

connectionCoreDeviceDesc: Nothing to install, and the smoothest live picture. Needs iOS 27 or later. Some banking apps take the live picture for screen sharing and refuse to run while Pinky is connected.

@connectionCoreDeviceDesc.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: what CoreDevice gives and costs.

connectionIOSTooOld: Pinky needs iOS 17.4 or later; this iPhone runs iOS {version}.

@connectionIOSTooOld.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: why no way works on this iPhone. version is its iOS version.

connectionNeedsIOS27: Needs iOS 27 or later; this iPhone runs iOS {version}.

@connectionNeedsIOS27.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: why CoreDevice cannot be used. version is the iPhone's iOS version.

connectionNoAnswer: The iPhone doesn't answer right now.

@connectionNoAnswer.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: why a way cannot be checked.

connectionNotInstalled: The helper isn't installed on this iPhone. Install it once with Xcode (WebDriverAgent's WebDriverAgentRunner, Product › Test); Pinky starts it after that.

@connectionNotInstalled.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: why the WebDriverAgent helper cannot be used yet, and how to install it. WebDriverAgent, WebDriverAgentRunner and Product › Test are names in Xcode.

@connectionOffline.description: The phone page header's second line and Settings › Phones, for an offline phone. platform is Android, iPhone or a version such as Android 16.

@connectionReadOnly.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: what Automatic picked on an iPhone below iOS 27 without the WebDriverAgent helper, where Pinky can read the screen but not act. Shown inside connectionAutoNow, so lower case.

@connectionReconnecting.description: A toast once an iPhone's connection was changed: Pinky reconnects it. phone is the phone's name.

@connectionTitle.description: Settings › Phones: the heading of an iPhone's choice of how Pinky connects to it.

@connectionWDA.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: the way through the WebDriverAgent helper app. WebDriverAgent is a name.

connectionWDADesc: Works from iOS 17.4, and shares no screen, so banking apps that refuse screen sharing keep working. Needs the helper installed once from Xcode, and now and then iOS asks on the iPhone for its passcode before the helper starts. The live picture and reading the screen are slower.

@connectionWDADesc.description: Settings › Phones, an iPhone's connection choice: what the WebDriverAgent helper gives and costs.

@dayOtherYear.description: Activity's heading of a day in another year: the month, day and year.

@dayThisYear.description: Activity's heading of a day earlier this year: the weekday, month and day.

@dayToday.description: Activity groups tasks by day: the heading of today's.

@dayYesterday.description: Activity groups tasks by day: the heading of yesterday's.

@exportAll.description: The button in Activity's header that exports every finished task into a new folder on the Desktop.

exportAllTooltip: Every finished task, as a report and JSON

@exportAllTooltip.description: The tooltip of Export all: what it writes, an HTML report and a JSON file.

@exportDone.description: A toast after an export, which also shows the report in the Finder. folder is the new folder's name (see exportFolderName); parent is the name of the folder it was made in: "Desktop", the Desktop folder's real name, which the Finder shows translated, or else the home folder's name. A translation may name the Desktop in its own words when parent is "Desktop", with a select.

@exportFailed.description: A toast when an export fails. detail is the error, in English.

@exportFolderAll.description: Export all: the word that names what it exported in the name of the folder it makes, "Pinky activity 2026-11-07 at 09.30.12" (see exportFolderName). Part of a file name.

@exportFolderName.description: The name of the folder an export makes on the Desktop. name is exportFolderAll or the exported task's title; date is as 2026-11-07, clock as 09.30.12 (with dots: file names cannot hold colons). It must stay a valid file name, without / or:.

@exportTask.description: An item of the ⋯ menu in a task's detail: exports that task into a new folder on the Desktop.

feedbackAttach: Attach diagnostics: versions, settings, phone models and Pinky's recent logs

@feedbackAttach.description: Send feedback: the checkbox that attaches the diagnostics (in English) to the issue.

feedbackBrowserFailed: Couldn't open the browser: {detail}. Copy the feedback and send it another way.

@feedbackBrowserFailed.description: Send feedback when the browser would not open; detail is the system's error in English.

@feedbackCancel.description: Send feedback: the button that closes the dialog, keeping the draft.

@feedbackCopied.description: A toast after copying the feedback.

@feedbackCopy.description: Send feedback: the button that copies the feedback.

feedbackCut: Not all of the logs fit in the link: Copy puts everything on the clipboard to paste into the issue.

@feedbackCut.description: Follows feedbackNote when the diagnostics are too long for the issue's link.

@feedbackHide.description: Send feedback: the button that hides the diagnostics again.

feedbackIntro: What happened, or what would make Pinky better? If something went wrong, say what you were doing.

@feedbackMessageField.description: Send feedback: the accessibility label of the message field.

@feedbackMessagePlaceholder.description: Send feedback: the message field's placeholder.

feedbackNote: Pinky opens a new issue on GitHub with this filled in; read it there and submit it with your GitHub account. Issues are public.

@feedbackNote.description: Send feedback: where the feedback goes, above the buttons.

@feedbackOpen.description: Send feedback: the button that opens the new issue in the browser.

feedbackRedacted: Phone names and IDs, your user name, e-mail and IP addresses, app and task names are taken out.

@feedbackRedacted.description: Send feedback: under the checkbox, what the diagnostics leave out.

@feedbackReview.description: Send feedback: the button that shows the diagnostics.

feedbackThanks: Finish your feedback on GitHub. Thanks!

@feedbackThanks.description: A toast after the new issue opened in the browser.

@feedbackTitle.description: The title and accessibility label of the Send feedback dialog.

@feedbackTitleField.description: Send feedback: the accessibility label of the title field.

@feedbackTitlePlaceholder.description: Send feedback: the title field's placeholder.

@flyoutLocked.description: Menu bar flyout: what a locked phone's Needs you row says after the phone's name.

@flyoutMenuStopAll.description: Item of the menu bar icon's menu: stops every agent on every phone at once.

@flyoutNeedLabel.description: The accessibility label of a Needs you row in the menu bar flyout: the phone and what waits for the person.

@flyoutNoPhones.description: Menu bar flyout: in place of the phones when there are none.

@flyoutOpenPinky.description: Item of the menu bar icon's menu and row of the menu bar flyout: shows Pinky's main window.

@flyoutPhoneLabel.description: The accessibility label of a phone's row in the menu bar flyout: its name and status line.

@flyoutPhones.description: Menu bar flyout: the heading above the phones.

@flyoutReview.description: Menu bar flyout: the action at the end of a Needs you row; a click opens the approval.

@flyoutShowPhones.description: Item of the menu bar icon's menu (the only way to it on Linux, whose tray icons get no clicks): opens the flyout with the phones.

@flyoutStopAll.description: The menu bar flyout's last row, in red, with its shortcut: stops every agent on every phone at once.

flyoutTrayTooltip: Pinky · {count, plural, one {# thing needs you} other {# things need you}}

@flyoutTrayTooltip.description: The tooltip of Pinky's menu bar icon while approvals, handoffs or locked phones wait for the person.

@flyoutUnlock.description: Menu bar flyout: the action at the end of a locked phone's Needs you row; a click opens the phone to unlock it.

foundDetail: It's on the same Wi-Fi as this computer and was set up before to connect to it over Wi-Fi, in Finder, Xcode or Pinky. Pinky hasn't used it, so it leaves it alone until you say it's yours: it doesn't connect to it, change anything on it or let agents use it.

@foundDetail.description: Under foundTitle, and in Add phone and the checkup: why Pinky waits for the person.

@foundIgnore.description: The button that leaves a phone Pinky found on Wi-Fi alone: it goes off the list until it is plugged in.

@foundIgnoreFailed.description: A notice when choosing Ignore for a phone found on Wi-Fi failed. name is the phone's name, error what went wrong.

@foundIgnoreLabel.description: What assistive technology reads for foundIgnore. name is the phone's name.

foundIgnoreNote: If you ignore it, it stays off the list until you plug it into this computer.

@foundIgnoreNote.description: Under the Use and Ignore buttons of a phone found on Wi-Fi.

foundIgnored: Ignoring {name}. To use it after all, plug it in.

@foundIgnored.description: A notice after the person chose Ignore for a phone found on Wi-Fi. name is the phone's name.

@foundTitle.description: The page of a phone Pinky found on Wi-Fi and has not used. phone is its name.

@foundUse.description: The button that lets Pinky use a phone it found on Wi-Fi: the person says it is theirs. Pinky then sets it up and connects to it.

@foundUseFailed.description: A notice when choosing Use for a phone found on Wi-Fi failed. name is the phone's name, error what went wrong.

@foundUseLabel.description: What assistive technology reads for foundUse. name is the phone's name.

foundUseNote: Pinky then sets it up over Wi-Fi; a step that needs the cable says so.

@foundUseNote.description: Under the Use and Ignore buttons of a phone found on Wi-Fi: what Use does.

@guideHonorAbout.description: Add phone › Android, step 1 on HONOR phones: where the item to tap 7 times is. Write it as menu names joined by ›, as the phone shows them in Simplified Chinese.

guideHonorAboutNote: Only the phone's owner can turn it on: not in a second user or a private space.

@guideHonorAboutNote.description: Add phone › Android, step 1 on HONOR phones: a note under the steps.

@guideHonorDev.description: Add phone › Android, step 2 on HONOR phones: where Developer options is once it is on. Write it as menu names joined by ›, as the phone shows them in Simplified Chinese.

guideHonorNote: If the phone asks what to use USB for, pick Transfer files.

@guideHonorNote.description: Add phone › Android, step 2 on HONOR phones: a note under the switches.

@guideHonorPromptAlways.description: Add phone › Android, step 3 on HONOR phones: the check box of HONOR's prompt to allow USB debugging. Use HONOR's Simplified Chinese words.

guideHonorSwitchCharge: Allow ADB debugging in charge only mode

@guideHonorSwitchCharge.description: Add phone › Android, step 2 on HONOR phones: HONOR's switch that keeps USB debugging on. Use the name of HONOR's Simplified Chinese settings, as written there.

@gwStepListedFolder.description: A step: the agent listed the files in the phone's Pinky folder. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepOutside.description: A step outside what the person allowed the agent. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepReceivedFile.description: A step: the agent sent a file (phone_files upload), which Pinky saved in the folder on the computer that is copied to the phone. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepUnlocked.description: A step: the phone was unlocked from this computer with its saved PIN. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepWaited.description: A step: the agent waited for this text to show on the screen. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepWaiting.description: A step that waits for the person's approval; action is gwDoTap and the like.

@gwStepYouAllowed.description: A step of the demo's fake gateway: the person allowed an action. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepYouDenied.description: A step of the demo's fake gateway: the person denied an action. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepYouStopped.description: A step of the demo's fake gateway: the person stopped the task. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepYouTookOver.description: A step of the demo's fake gateway: the person took over. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwStepYourNote.description: The second line of a step: the note the person gave with an answer, in quotes. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

gwUnlockDetail: {agent} is waiting for the phone to unlock · {task}

@gwUnlockDetail.description: The second line of the unlock card. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@gwUnlockTitle.description: The title of the card that asks the person to unlock a locked phone an agent waits for. Shown only in other languages; in English the gateway's own words show.

@listMany.description: Three or more names in a sentence: rest is the names before the last, joined with listSeparator.

@listPair.description: Two names in a sentence, as "Can use Dinely and Chatter".

@listSeparator.description: Joins the names of a list before its last one (see listMany).

@lostConfirmButton.description: The button of the dialog that restarts macOS's device service.

lostConfirmMessage: Pinky restarts macOS's device service, usbmuxd, so that it looks for {phone} again. Every iPhone and iPad connected to this Mac, also on a cable, disconnects for a second or two, and tasks on them wait. Then macOS asks for an administrator's password.

@lostConfirmMessage.description: The message of the dialog that asks before Pinky restarts macOS's device service. phone is the lost iPhone's name.

@lostConfirmTitle.description: The dialog that asks before Pinky restarts macOS's device service.

lostDetail: {phone} is on the same Wi-Fi, but macOS's device service (usbmuxd) stopped listing it after its connection broke once, and may not list it again for up to an hour. Restarting the service makes it look again.

@lostDetail.description: Under lostTitle, and in Add phone and the checkup. phone is its name.

lostManual: Or restart it yourself: run sudo killall usbmuxd in Terminal.

@lostManual.description: Under the restart button, or in its place where Pinky cannot restart the service itself.

lostReason: Pinky wants to restart the device service (usbmuxd) so that this Mac finds your iPhone on Wi-Fi again.

@lostReason.description: Shown in macOS's own request for an administrator's password when Pinky restarts the device service.

@lostRestart.description: The button that restarts macOS's device service (usbmuxd) so it finds a lost iPhone again; it asks first.

@lostRestartFailed.description: A notice when restarting macOS's device service failed. error is what went wrong.

lostRestartNote: Every iPhone and iPad connected to this Mac, also on a cable, disconnects for a second or two. macOS asks for an administrator's password.

@lostRestartNote.description: Under the Restart device service button.

lostRestarted: Restarted the device service. {phone} shows up again in a few seconds.

@lostRestarted.description: A notice after Pinky restarted macOS's device service. phone is the lost iPhone's name.

@lostTitle.description: The page of an iPhone that macOS's device service stopped listing though it is on the same Wi-Fi. phone is its name.

@menuPhones.description: The menu bar's menu of the app's pages and Stop all.

@menuStopAll.description: Phones menu: stops every agent on every phone.

@mirrorAgentScreenLabel.description: The accessibility label of the mirror while it shows the agent's own screen: the hidden second screen it works on in the background. agent is the agent's name, or "The agent" (agentGenericStart); phone is the phone's name.

@mirrorCallKey.description: A verb phrase that completes the toast "Couldn't …: <error>" when a key pressed on the mirror cannot reach the phone. key is the phone's name for the key, in English: back, home, enter, tab, delete, escape, dpad_up, page_down…

@mirrorCallPaste.description: A verb phrase that completes the toast "Couldn't …: <error>" when ⌘V on the mirror cannot paste the Mac's clipboard on the phone.

@mirrorCallTouch.description: A verb phrase that completes the toast "Couldn't …: <error>" when a click, drag or scroll on the mirror cannot reach the phone.

@mirrorCallType.description: A verb phrase that completes the toast "Couldn't …: <error>" when text typed on the mirror cannot reach the phone.

@mirrorConnecting.description: Under a spinner over the mirror while the phone's live picture connects.

@mirrorDecoderSoftware.description: Settings › Advanced in Developer mode, the Video row: how a mirror decodes without a hardware decoder, in place of a hardware decoder's name such as videotoolbox (see mirrorDecoderStats).

@mirrorDecoderStats.description: Settings › Advanced in Developer mode, the Video row: adds a playing mirror to the line. line is the line so far (FFmpeg's libavcodec version and the mirrors before); device is the phone's ID; decoder is mirrorDecoderSoftware or a hardware decoder's name; fps is pictures per second; latency is the time from a packet's arrival to its picture.

@mirrorLocked.description: A pill over the dimmed mirror of a locked phone. phone is the phone's name. One line over the phone's picture: keep it short.

@mirrorLockedTile.description: The same pill over a locked phone's tile in All phones, which can be 168 points wide.

@mirrorNoPicture.description: Over the mirror when the phone's live picture fails. detail is the error, in English.

@mirrorOffline.description: Over the mirror when the phone disconnected.

@mirrorScreenLabel.description: The accessibility label of the mirror, the phone's live picture, where clicks, scrolls and typing reach the phone. phone is the phone's name.

@mirrorStreamEnded.description: Over the mirror when the phone's live picture stopped; it connects again by itself.

mirrorUnsupported: This phone has no live picture.

@mirrorUnsupported.description: Over the mirror of a phone that cannot stream its screen.

@needsAddNote.description: Link on a handoff card that opens a field for a note to the agent.

needsAgentAskedReadOnly: {agent} asked to only browse and read.

@needsAgentAskedReadOnly.description: On an agent's first-connection card, above the menu of what it may do, when the agent asked to only browse and read (phone_connect read_only). The menu then starts on scopeReadOnly.

@needsAllow.description: Primary button that allows the step once: on approval cards and in the floating approval panel.

@needsAllowTask.description: Item of More options: allow steps like this one until the agent's task ends.

@needsAlwaysAllow.description: Item of More options: never ask again for steps like this one. kind says what they are, from the rule that asked, or "this kind" when no rule is named.

@needsAlwaysAllowIn.description: Item of More options on an approval card: never ask again for steps like this one in this app. kind says what they are, from the rule that asked; app is the app's name.

@needsAndTasksLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Phones page's right-hand column, which holds the Needs you cards and the Tasks.

@needsApprove.description: Primary button on an agent's first-connection card: lets the agent use the phones as chosen above it.

@needsApproveNoApps.description: The tooltip of the disabled Approve button on a first-connection card, when "Only the apps I choose" is chosen and no app is named yet.

@needsDecline.description: Button (or link) on a handoff card: tells the agent the person won't do what it asked.

@needsDeclineTooltip.description: The tooltip of Decline on a handoff card.

@needsDeny.description: Button that denies an approval or an agent's first connection: on Needs you cards and in the floating approval panel.

needsDenyNotePlaceholder: Why not, or what to do instead

@needsDenyNotePlaceholder.description: The placeholder of the note field after Deny with a note, on an approval card: why the person said no, or what the agent should do instead.

@needsDenyWithNote.description: Item of More options: opens a field for a note to the agent, then Deny sends it with the answer.

@needsDone.description: Button on a handoff card: the person did what the agent asked, and the phone goes back to the agent, with the note if there is one.

@needsDoneTooltip.description: The tooltip of Done on a handoff card.

@needsFirstConnection.description: The small line above a card's title when an agent connects for the first time and asks to use the phones. Other cards show the phone and app there, as "Pixel 9 · Dinely".

needsHandoffHowTo: Do it on the phone and click Done, or take over to do it here.

@needsHandoffHowTo.description: A handoff card: the agent asked the person to do something on the phone (its request is the card's title). Done and Take over are the card's buttons.

needsHandoffInControl: You're in control. Click Done to hand the phone back to {agent}.

@needsHandoffInControl.description: A handoff card (the agent asked the person to do something on the phone, its request is the title) after the person took over. Done is the card's button (needsDone).

@needsHandoffLocked.description: A handoff card on a locked phone that this computer cannot unlock. how is a sentence that says how to unlock it, ending with needsThenClickDone.

how.example: Unlock it on the phone, then click Done.

needsHandoffLockedHere: The phone is locked. Unlocking it here hands it back to {agent}. If you unlock it on the phone, click Done when you're finished.

@needsHandoffLockedHere.description: A handoff card on a locked phone that this computer can unlock, under the Unlock with Touch ID button. Done is the card's button (needsDone).

needsHandoffLockedHereThenDone: The phone is locked. Unlock it here or on the phone, do what {agent} asked, then click Done.

@needsHandoffLockedHereThenDone.description: A handoff card on a locked phone that this computer can unlock, under the Unlock with Touch ID button, when the agent asked for more than unlocking: unlocking does not hand the phone back. Done is the card's button (needsDone).

needsHandoffNotePlaceholder: What you did, or what to do next

@needsHandoffNotePlaceholder.description: The placeholder of the note field on a handoff card: what the person did on the phone, or what the agent should do next.

needsHandoffSetup: Do it as asked. Once the phone is ready, {agent} goes on by itself.

@needsHandoffSetup.description: A handoff card, when the agent asked the person to do the setup step the phone waits for (such as trusting the computer; its request is the title): there is nothing to take over, and the agent goes on by itself once the phone is ready.

@needsLetAgent.description: On an agent's first-connection card: the label above (and the accessibility label of) the menu of what the agent may do. In English it reads on into the choice: "Let Claude Code" + "All apps except blocked ones", "Only the apps I choose", "Read only: browse, never commit" or "Watch only: no taps or typing".

@needsMoreOptions.description: Link under Deny and Allow, on approval cards and in the floating approval panel, that opens a menu: Allow for this task, Always allow …, Take over, Deny with a note.

@needsNoteFor.description: The label above (and the accessibility label of) the field where the person writes a note to the agent: on handoff and approval cards and in the floating approval panel.

@needsSection.description: The heading (and accessibility label) of the cards that wait for the person (approvals, handoffs, locked phones): in the right-hand column and in the menu bar flyout.

needsTakeOverTooltip: Do it here, in the mirror

@needsTakeOverTooltip.description: The tooltip of Take over on a handoff card: the person does what the agent asked in the app's live picture of the phone.

@needsThenClickDone.description: Ends the sentence that says how to unlock a phone on a handoff card ("Unlock it on the phone, then click Done."): it starts with a comma and ends the sentence. Done is the card's button (needsDone).

needsUnblockHow: {app} is blocked by “{rule}”. Allowing lets {agent} open it and read its screen until this task ends. What your rules ask about still asks, Pinky keeps no screenshots or recordings of it (it reads text from its screen without keeping a picture), and it stays blocked in Settings.

@needsUnblockHow.description: On the card that asks whether an agent may open a blocked app for its task, above Deny and needsAllowTask. rule is the rule that blocks it, such as Finance apps.

@pairingAddrField.description: Pair with a code: the label above the field for the address the phone shows (as 192.168.1.20:37123), and the field's accessibility label.

pairingAddrInvalid: Enter the IP address and port the phone shows, like 192.168.1.20:37123.

@pairingAddrInvalid.description: Pair with a code: the error under the form when the address typed is not an IP address and port.

@pairingBusy.description: Pair with a code: next to a spinner, right of the Pair button, while Pinky pairs.

pairingCodeDetail: On the phone, open Developer options › Wireless debugging and tap Pair device with pairing code. Enter what it shows.

@pairingCodeDetail.description: Pair with a code: the line under the heading. Developer options, Wireless debugging and Pair device with pairing code are Android's own names: use those of Android's Simplified Chinese settings.

@pairingCodeField.description: Pair with a code: the label above the field for the six-digit pairing code the phone shows, and the field's accessibility label.

pairingCodeIncomplete: Enter the six-digit code the phone shows.

@pairingCodeIncomplete.description: Pair with a code: the error under the form when the code typed has fewer than six digits.

@pairingCodePlaceholder.description: Pair with a code: the placeholder of the pairing code field, a narrow field.

@pairingCodeTitle.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the heading of the form that pairs with the address and the six-digit code the phone shows.

@pairingConnect.description: Pair with a code: the button that connects to the address typed in the connect step.

@pairingConnectBusy.description: Pair with a code: next to a spinner, right of the Connect button, while Pinky connects.

pairingConnectDetail: The phone paired, but Pinky can't find it on this network. On the phone, open Wireless debugging and enter the IP address and port shown at the top.

@pairingConnectDetail.description: Pair with a code: the line under pairingConnectTitle. Wireless debugging is Android's own name.

@pairingConnectErrOther.description: Pair with a code: the error when connecting in the connect step failed for another reason. detail is the error, in English.

pairingConnectErrUnreachable: Couldn't connect at that address. Use the IP address and port at the top of Wireless debugging, not the ones of the pairing dialog.

@pairingConnectErrUnreachable.description: Pair with a code: the error when nothing answered at the address typed in the connect step. Wireless debugging is Android's own name.

@pairingConnectTitle.description: Pair with a code: the heading of the step that connects to a phone that paired but that Pinky could not find on the network.

@pairingConnecting.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the status line, next to a spinner, once the phone paired and Pinky connects to it.

pairingErrNoAdb: Android's adb isn't working on this computer, so Pinky can't pair phones over Wi-Fi. Go back to see why, or use a USB cable.

@pairingErrNoAdb.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the error when adb does not work on this computer (no adb, or its server does not run); Add phone › Android, one step back, says why.

pairingErrNotListening: Nothing at that address is waiting to pair. Check the IP address and port in the Pair device with pairing code dialog, and keep it open until Pinky is done.

@pairingErrNotListening.description: Pair with a code: the error when nothing at the address typed took the connection (a wrong port, or the dialog closed). Pair device with pairing code is Android's own name.

@pairingErrOther.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the error when pairing failed for another reason. detail is the error, in English.

pairingErrQRNotListening: The phone stopped waiting to pair, as it does when it leaves the scanning screen. Scan the code again, or pair with a code instead.

@pairingErrQRNotListening.description: Pair over Wi-Fi by QR code: the error when the phone's pairing service no longer took the connection. Shown with pairingUseCode and addPhoneTryAgain.

pairingErrQRRejected: The phone ended the pairing before it finished. Keep the phone on the same Wi-Fi as this computer and on its scanning screen until Pinky is done, then try again, or pair with a code instead.

@pairingErrQRRejected.description: Pair over Wi-Fi by QR code: the error when the phone ended the pairing (adb cannot tell why; the code is Pinky's, so never say it was wrong). Shown with pairingUseCode and addPhoneTryAgain.

pairingErrQRUnreachable: The phone showed up on the network, but Pinky couldn't connect to it. A VPN or firewall on this computer, or a network that keeps devices apart, such as guest Wi-Fi, can block it. Try another network, or a USB cable.

@pairingErrQRUnreachable.description: Pair over Wi-Fi by QR code: the error when the phone showed up on the network but its pairing address did not answer.

pairingErrRejected: The phone didn't accept the pairing. Check the code, and that the port is the one in the Pair device with pairing code dialog, not the one at the top of Wireless debugging. Both change each time the dialog opens.

@pairingErrRejected.description: Pair with a code: the error when the phone ended the pairing, which adb reports the same way for a wrong code, a port that is not the pairing dialog's and a dropped connection. Pair device with pairing code and Wireless debugging are Android's own names.

pairingErrTimeout: The phone didn't answer in time. Check that it's on the same Wi-Fi as this computer and that Wireless debugging is on, then try again.

@pairingErrTimeout.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the error when the phone did not answer in time. Wireless debugging is Android's setting.

pairingErrUnreachable: Couldn't reach the phone at that address. Check the IP address and port under Pair device with pairing code; they change each time it opens.

@pairingErrUnreachable.description: Pair with a code: the error when the address typed did not answer. Pair device with pairing code is Android's own name.

pairingErrUnsupported: Pairing over Wi-Fi isn't available here. Use a USB cable instead.

@pairingErrUnsupported.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the error when the phone's driver cannot pair over Wi-Fi.

@pairingFound.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the status line, next to a spinner, once the phone scanned the code and Pinky pairs with it.

@pairingGettingCode.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the status line, next to a spinner, while Pinky gets the QR code from the gateway.

@pairingNoCode.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: in place of the QR code, under an alert icon, when getting one failed.

@pairingOpenLocalNetwork.description: Pair over Wi-Fi, on a Mac: the button under the note that opens System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network. Local Network is macOS's own name.

@pairingPair.description: Add phone: the button that pairs with the code typed, in the Android form "Pair with a code" and in the iPhone step.

@pairingPaired.description: A notice once a phone paired over Wi-Fi; its page opens. name is the phone's name.

@pairingPairedPhone.description: A notice once a phone paired over Wi-Fi, when its name is unknown.

pairingQRDetail: On the phone, open Developer options › Wireless debugging and tap Pair device with QR code, then scan this code. Keep the phone on the same Wi-Fi as this computer.

@pairingQRDetail.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the line under the heading, above the QR code. Developer options, Wireless debugging and Pair device with QR code are Android's own names: use those of Android's Simplified Chinese settings.

@pairingQRDrawError.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the status line when Pinky could not draw the QR code. detail is the error, in English.

pairingQRLabel: QR code to scan in Wireless debugging › Pair device with QR code

@pairingQRLabel.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the accessibility label of the QR code. Wireless debugging and Pair device with QR code are Android's own names.

pairingStuckNoSearch: Check that this computer is connected to Wi-Fi or Ethernet, or pair with a code instead. ({detail})

@pairingStuckNoSearch.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the note's text under pairingStuckNoSearchTitle. detail is the error, in English.

detail.example: mdns: no network interface to search

pairingStuckNoSearchTitle: Pinky can't look for phones on this network

@pairingStuckNoSearchTitle.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the heading of the note when Pinky cannot search the network for another reason, such as no network connection.

pairingStuckNotAllowed: Something on this computer, perhaps a firewall, keeps Pinky from looking for phones on the network. Let Pinky use the local network, or pair with a code instead.

@pairingStuckNotAllowed.description: Pair over Wi-Fi, on Linux and Windows: the note's text under pairingStuckNotAllowedTitle.

pairingStuckNotAllowedMac: Turn on Pinky under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network, then try again. Or pair with a code instead.

@pairingStuckNotAllowedMac.description: Pair over Wi-Fi, on a Mac: the note's text under pairingStuckNotAllowedTitle. System Settings, Privacy & Security and Local Network are macOS's own names: use those of macOS in Simplified Chinese.

pairingStuckNotAllowedTitle: Pinky isn't allowed to look for phones on this network

@pairingStuckNotAllowedTitle.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the heading of the note when the system keeps Pinky from looking for devices on the local network.

pairingStuckNotSeen: Scan this code on the phone under Wireless debugging › Pair device with QR code, with the phone on the same Wi-Fi as this computer. Some networks, such as guest Wi-Fi and many offices, keep devices from finding each other; there, pair with a code instead.

@pairingStuckNotSeen.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the note's text under pairingStuckNotSeenTitle. Wireless debugging and Pair device with QR code are Android's own names: use those of Android's Simplified Chinese settings.

pairingStuckNotSeenTitle: The phone hasn't shown up on the network yet

@pairingStuckNotSeenTitle.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the heading of the note under the status line when, 30 seconds after the code showed, the phone has not appeared on the network: it has not scanned the code, or the network keeps devices apart.

pairingStuckPairing: If the phone shows an error or went back to Wireless debugging, scan the code again. Or pair with a code instead.

@pairingStuckPairing.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the note's text under pairingStuckPairingTitle. Wireless debugging is Android's own name.

pairingStuckPairingTitle: The phone showed up, but pairing hasn't finished

@pairingStuckPairingTitle.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the heading of the note when the phone appeared on the network a while ago and pairing has not finished.

@pairingTitle.description: Add phone › Pair over Wi-Fi: the heading of the step that pairs an Android phone over Wi-Fi with a QR code.

pairingUnsupported: This gateway can't pair phones over Wi-Fi. Connect the phone with a USB cable instead.

@pairingUnsupported.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the line under the heading when the gateway Pinky uses cannot pair phones.

@pairingUseCode.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the link that switches from the QR code to typing the address and six-digit code the phone shows.

@pairingUseQR.description: Pair with a code: the link that switches back to the QR code.

@pairingUseUSB.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the link that goes back to connecting the phone with a USB cable.

pairingWaiting: Waiting for the phone to scan the code…

@pairingWaiting.description: Pair over Wi-Fi: the status line under the QR code, next to a spinner, while Pinky waits for the phone to scan it.

@panelActionsLikeThis.description: Stands for the rule's name in panelAllowedTaskDetail and panelAlwaysAllowedDetail when the approval names no rule.

panelAgentAllowed: {agent} can use your phones. Change what it may do in Settings › Agents.

@panelAgentAllowed.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Allowed, after the person approved an agent's first connection. Settings › Agents is the Settings section that lists the agents.

@panelAgentDenied.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Denied, after the person denied an agent's first connection.

@panelAllowed.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Approve on an agent's first connection.

@panelAllowedOnce.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Allow.

panelAllowedOnceDetail: Pinky checks the button is still on screen, then taps it.

@panelAllowedOnceDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Allowed once: what happens on the phone next.

@panelAllowedTask.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Allow for this task.

panelAllowedTaskDetail: {rule} in {app} are allowed until this task ends.

@panelAllowedTaskDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Allowed for this task. rule is the name of the rule that asked, or panelActionsLikeThis; app is the app's name, or panelThisApp.

@panelAlwaysAllowed.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Always allow ….

panelAlwaysAllowedDetail: {rule} in {app} no longer ask. Change it in Settings.

@panelAlwaysAllowedDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Always allowed: Pinky won't ask the person about these steps again. rule is the name of the rule that asked, or panelActionsLikeThis; app is the app's name, or panelThisApp.

@panelCancel.description: Button in the floating approval panel's note editor: back to the approval without denying it.

@panelDeclined.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Decline on a handoff.

@panelDenied.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Deny, on an approval or an agent's first connection.

panelDeniedDetail: Nothing was tapped. {agent} was told no.

@panelDeniedDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Denied, after the person denied a step.

panelDeniedDetailNote: Nothing was tapped. {agent} was told no, with your note: “{note}”

@panelDeniedDetailNote.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Denied, after the person denied a step with a note. note is the person's own words.

@panelDeniesIn.description: Top right of the floating approval panel: the approval is denied by itself when this time runs out. duration is as "42 s".

@panelDenyWithNote.description: Primary button in the floating approval panel's note editor: denies the approval and sends the note to the agent. Half of the 360-point panel's width.

@panelEndsIn.description: Top right of the floating approval panel for a handoff (the agent asked the person to do something): the request ends when this time runs out. duration is as "4 min 10 s".

@panelHandedBack.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation title after Done on a handoff: the phone went back to the agent.

@panelHandedBackDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Handed back.

@panelNext.description: The accessibility label of the floating approval panel's right arrow.

@panelPosition.description: The floating approval panel's pager, between its two arrows: which of the waiting approvals it shows. Keep it short.

@panelPrevious.description: The accessibility label of the floating approval panel's left arrow.

@panelShotLabel.description: The accessibility label of an approval's screenshot in the floating approval panel, on a Needs you card and in its large view: the phone's whole screen and the part around what the agent wants to tap, with that element marked.

@panelThisApp.description: Stands for the app's name in panelAllowedTaskDetail and panelAlwaysAllowedDetail when the approval names no app.

@panelToldNo.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under Declined: the agent learned that the person won't do what it asked.

panelUnblockedDetail: {agent} can use {app} until this task ends.

@panelUnblockedDetail.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation under panelAllowedTask, after the person allowed a blocked app for the agent's task.

@panelWaitingApprovals.description: The accessibility label of the floating approval panel's pager (previous, "1 of 2", next) when several approvals wait.

@panelWindowTitle.description: The title of the floating approval panel's window. The panel has no title bar; screen readers and window lists read it.

@panelWithNote.description: The floating approval panel's confirmation after a handoff was answered with a note: text is the confirmation's sentence (panelHandedBackDetail or panelToldNo), note the person's own words.

text.example: Claude Code goes on from here.

@phoneAddPhone.description: Primary button on the Phones page before any phone is added: opens Add phone.

@phoneAgentScreen.description: Choice of the switch under the mirror while an agent works on a hidden second screen: the mirror shows the agent's screen.

@phoneAllPhones.description: The Phones page's title when it shows every phone as live tiles.

phoneAwayOff: {name} stopped taking connections from afar, as it does when the phone restarts. When it's near this computer again, turn Use away from home on again in Settings › Phones.

@phoneAwayOff.description: An offline phone's page, for a phone used away from home whose adb stopped listening.

phoneBackgroundDesc: Agents use a hidden second screen, so the phone stays yours and can stay locked. From the next task.

@phoneBackgroundDesc.description: Under Work in the background in ⋯ under the mirror: what the switch does, and that it applies from the agent's next task.

phoneBackgroundUnsupported: This phone can't give agents a second screen.

@phoneBackgroundUnsupported.description: Under Work in the background in ⋯, when the phone can't do it (the switch is disabled).

phoneBannerHandBackHint: Hand back to let agents use this phone again.

@phoneBannerHandBackHint.description: The banner above the mirror, after the bold phoneBannerInControl, when no agent waits: Hand back is the banner's button.

@phoneBannerInControl.description: The bold start of the banner above the mirror while the person controls the phone; the rest follows in normal weight (phoneBannerPaused or phoneBannerHandBackHint). English ends with a space before the rest.

@phoneBannerPaused.description: The banner above the mirror, after the bold phoneBannerInControl: the agent waits until the person hands the phone back.

@unlockCallWhat.description: Fills "Couldn't …: <error>", a notice when unlocking a phone fails: a verb phrase.

@unlockEnd.description: Ends the hints that say how to unlock a phone on it (the unlockOnPhone messages) when nothing follows them: a full stop.

@unlockErrNoPIN.description: A notice when unlocking failed because no PIN is saved for the phone. name is the phone's name.

unlockErrNoPad: Pinky couldn't get to {name}'s passcode screen, so it entered nothing. Try again, or unlock it on the phone.

unlockErrNoUnlock: Unlocking from this computer isn't available. Unlock {name} on the phone.

@unlockErrNoUnlock.description: A notice when the gateway cannot unlock phones. name is the phone's name.

unlockErrUnsupported: {name} can't be unlocked from this computer. Unlock it on the phone.

@unlockErrWrongPIN.description: A notice when the phone refused its saved PIN. Pinky stops trying it, as phones lock out, or erase themselves, after repeated wrong PINs. name is the phone's name; Settings › Phones is Pinky's Settings page.

unlockFromHere: Unlock it from here when you or an agent need it.

@unlockLocked.description: The title of the card on a locked phone's side panel, next to a lock icon, and the card's accessibility label. name is the phone's name.

unlockNotAvailable: Unlocking from this computer is not available on this system.

@unlockNotNowLabel.description: The accessibility label of the Not now button on the locked phone's card. name is the phone's name.

unlockOnPhoneOff: Unlock it on the phone{end} Unlocking from this computer is off in Settings › Safety.

unlockOnPhoneSavePIN: Save the phone's PIN to unlock it from this computer, or unlock it on the phone{end}

unlockOnPhoneWrongPIN: The saved PIN didn't unlock it, so Pinky won't try it again. Unlock it on the phone{end} If its PIN changed, update it in Settings › Phones.

@unlockOnPhoneWrongPIN.description: The locked phone's card, after the phone refused its saved PIN: Pinky won't try it again. end as in unlockOnPhone.

wiFiNoWiFi: {name} isn't on Wi-Fi. Connect it to the same Wi-Fi as this computer.

@wiFiOffDesc.description: Under wiFiTitle while it is off. Wireless debugging is Android's own name.
